docs.title: SRToolkit: Symbolic Regression / Equation Discovery Benchmark Toolkit
docs.text: Documentation:: https://smeznar.github.io/SymbolicRegressionToolkit

docs.title: What is SRToolkit?
docs.text: The SRToolkit is a comprehensive Python toolkit designed to accelerate research and development in Symbolic Regression (SR) / Equation Discovery (ED). It provides a robust, easy-to-use framework for benchmarking, rapid prototyping, and mathematical expression manipulation.

docs.title: Core Features
docs.text:
SRToolkit provides a straightforward interface for:

  • Implementing new Symbolic Regression approaches and evaluating their performance against other approaches.

  • Benchmarking Symbolic Regression approaches using built-in benchmarks (currently Feynman and Nguyen) or custom data.

  • Experiment organization and postprocessing of results.

  • Converting expressions into expression trees or fast, callable NumPy functions.

  • Generating random expressions by defining the symbol space or a grammar.

  • Estimating constant parameters of expressions against real-world data.

  • Comparing and measuring the distance between expressions.

docs.title: Installation
docs.text:
To install the latest stable release of the package, run the following command in your terminal: 

pip install symbolic-regression-toolkit

Some built-in approaches (currently EDHiE) require extra dependencies (PyTorch and pymoo). To install them alongside the package, use the approaches extra: 

pip install 'symbolic-regression-toolkit[approaches]'

Alternatively, you can install the latest build directly from the repository with the command (Recommended):

pip install git+https://github.com/smeznar/SymbolicRegressionToolkit

docs.title: 1. Expression Manipulation (The Toolkit Core)
docs.text:
SRToolkit offers fundamental utilities for working with mathematical expressions as tokens, trees, and executable code—the building blocks for any SR approach.

import numpy as np
from SRToolkit.utils import compile_expr, tokens_to_tree, SymbolLibrary, expr_to_latex

# Create an executable function from the expression
expr = compile_expr(["X_0", "+", "X_1", "*", "C"])

# Calculate the output at two points (1, 2) and (2, 5) with C=3
data_points = np.array([[1, 2], [2, 5]])
constants = [3]
output = expr(data_points, constants)
# Variable "output" should now contain np.array([7, 17])

# Use a SymbolLibrary as a context manager to avoid passing it to every call
with SymbolLibrary.default_symbols(num_variables=2) as sl:
    # Create an expression tree from the token list
    expr_tree = tokens_to_tree(["X_0", "+", "X_1", "*", "C"])

    # Transform the expression into a list of symbols in postfix notation
    postfix_expr = expr_tree.to_list(notation="postfix")

    # Create a LaTeX string of the expression for clear presentation
    expr_latex = expr_to_latex(expr_tree)

docs.title: 2. Benchmarking and Evaluation (The Main Use Case)
docs.text:
The primary advantage of SRToolkit is its robust benchmarking framework, allowing you to quickly evaluate and compare different Symbolic Regression approaches.

from SRToolkit.approaches import EDHiE, ProGED
from SRToolkit.dataset import Feynman
from SRToolkit.evaluation import LoggingCallback
from SRToolkit.experiments import ExperimentGrid

# Load the Feynman benchmark and pick two 2-variable datasets to run on.
bm = Feynman()
ds_names = bm.list_datasets(num_variables=2, verbose=False)
dataset1 = bm.create_dataset(ds_names[0])
dataset2 = bm.create_dataset(ds_names[1])

# Define the SR approaches to benchmark.
# EDHiE requires a pre-trained/adapted model state; ProGED needs no time consuming adaptation.
edhie = EDHiE()
proged = ProGED()

# Map each (approach, dataset) pair to a file where the adapted model state will
# be saved. Both datasets reuse the same file here because they share the same
# number of variables, so one adapted state covers both.
adapted_states = {edhie.name: {ds_names[0]: "edhie_2v.pt", ds_names[1]: "edhie_2v.pt"}}

# Build the experiment grid: every combination of approach × dataset will be run
# num_experiments times (with different random seeds). Results are written under
# results_dir, specifically to "results_dir/{dataset}/{approach}/exp_{seed}.json".
eg = ExperimentGrid(
    approaches=[proged, edhie],
    datasets=[dataset1, dataset2],
    num_experiments=2,
    results_dir="results",
    adapted_states=adapted_states,
)

# Write a shell script of CLI commands that can be executed in parallel, e.g.:
#   cat commands.sh | parallel -j 4
eg.save_commands("commands.sh")

# Run adaptation for any approach/dataset pair whose adapted state file is missing.
# This is a no-op if all state files already exist.
eg.adapt_if_missing()

# Collect all pending jobs (skip any whose result file already exists on disk).
jobs = eg.create_jobs(skip_completed=True)

# Run each job sequentially in this process. To parallelize, use the generated
# commands.sh instead.
for job in jobs:
    job.run()

# See how many jobs are completed
eg.progress()

Additional examples can be found in the examples folder or in the official documentation.

docs.title: Roadmap 🗺️
docs.text:
In future releases, our primary focus will:

  • Expanded Library of Approaches: Add more Symbolic Regression approaches to the toolkit.

  • Result Visualization: Implement a robust visualization and result aggregation framework for SR results.

  • Simplification: Implement a better (more accurate, efficient, and stable) simplification system for expressions.

  • Constraints: Implement more robust expression generation constraints using techniques like attribute grammars.

  • Improved Benchmarking: Improve the robustness and efficiency of the benchmarking framework (continuous).

  • Advanced Expressions (Distant Plan): Implement support for different types of expressions, such as ODEs and PDEs.

docs.title: Contributing 🤝
docs.text:
We welcome contributions! Whether you're adding a new benchmark, implementing an SR approach, fixing a bug, or improving the documentation, please feel free to open a issue on the Github page or submit a Pull Request (PR) with a clear description of your changes.

We are especially looking for contributions of:

  • New Benchmarks and Datasets.

  • Implementations of additional Symbolic Regression Approaches (once the core framework for comparison is finalized).

Instructions on how to contribute can be found in the Contribution Guide.

docs.title: SymbolicRegressionToolkit (unreleased)
docs.text:
• Ranking functions are now pluggable: RankingFunction with the built-in RMSERanking and BEDRanking. SR_evaluator and SR_dataset accept a built-in name ("rmse", "bed") or the import path of a custom ranking.
  • Datasets can carry a held-out test set (test_X / test_y, dataset.test) and extra data for your own measures (aux_data), stored as DataSplits. Both are saved, cached and shared with the dataset, and can be regenerated from their own data source.
  • New HoldoutMetric augmenter scores results on held-out data. It reuses the constants fitted during the search by default; refit_constants=True refits them on the held-out data instead.
  • BED:
  • takes its evaluation points from the samplers setting (the input distribution) when its behaviour comes from a ground-truth expression and num_points_sampled is not -1, otherwise from X; datasets always pass their samplers;
  • can rank expressions against the observed targets y when no ground-truth expression is given;
  • is fixed per dataset by default (ranking_seed, the dataset's seed), so every run on a dataset is scored by the same objective; bed_resample=True resamples it per run.
  • Added an rmse regression metric.
  • Python 3.14 support: wheels are built for 3.10–3.14, and CI tests all five versions.
  • Removed the editdistance dependency (no wheels for Python ≥ 3.13); edit_distance now uses a pure-Python Levenshtein implementation.
  • Installing from source without a C compiler now works as documented: the Cython extension is skipped and the pure-Python evaluator is used. A RuntimeWarning is issued the first time the "stack" backend falls back, and SRToolkit.utils.expression_compiler.CYTHON_AVAILABLE tells which evaluator is in use. Set SRTOOLKIT_REQUIRE_CYTHON=1 to make a failed build an error.
  • SR_results can be iterated over directly (for result in results:); previously such a loop ended with an AssertionError (#5).
  • SymbolLibrary(symbols, ...) and SymbolLibrary.from_symbol_list raise a ValueError for names that are not default tokens (e.g. a whole expression such as "x/(a + x)", or X_3 with num_variables=1) instead of silently dropping them (#7). The add_symbol docs show how to add a fixed composite function such as x / (1 + x) as a custom token.
  • Results record the evaluation trace: EvalResult.trace lists, for every counted evaluate_expr call, the index into all_models of the requested expression (cache hits included). New EvalResult.best_so_far(), calls_to_threshold(threshold=None) and best_error_within(budgets) compute the incumbent history, the number of calls needed to reach a threshold, and the best error within given budgets.
  • import SRToolkit no longer imports PyTorch: EDHiE and EDHiEConfig are loaded the first time they are used. This cuts the import's memory use from about 770 MB to 150 MB and makes it faster.
  • PredictFn, the type of the predict argument of the regression metrics, is exported from SRToolkit.utils.
  • create_behavior_matrix and bed take a backend argument (default "stack"), and BED ranking now respects the backend setting, which previously only applied to RMSE ranking and get_metric.
  • The docstrings of SRToolkit.utils.measures now fully specify each function: valid inputs, special values (nan, inf), exceptions, and how bed handles non-finite values.
  • Saved results and configs (ModelResult, EvalResult, ApproachConfig, HoldoutMetric) now round-trip exactly: numpy arrays keep their dtype and shape (including empty axes such as (0, 3)) and object arrays are saved element by element, tuples stay tuples, and dicts with non-string keys (int, float, tuple, numpy scalars) keep their keys. Files written by earlier versions still load. The supported values and the file format are documented on the new SRToolkit.utils.serialization reference page.
  • Expression constraints (SRToolkit.utils.expression_constraints): ExpressionConstraint checks a candidate before scoring (pre_check, on the expression) and/or after (post_check, on the fitted model), and returns a CheckResult (passed, message, amount). Built-ins: MaxConstants, MaxTokens, MaxTreeDepth, MaxTreeSize, RequiredVariables, MaxSymbolCount, NoNesting and OutputBounds. OutputBounds takes one bound for all points or one per point. A check that raises counts as failed: its CheckResult has error set, a required constraint then gives status "error", and an advisory one is recorded in advisory_violations.
  • SR_evaluator takes required_constraints (a failed check gives status "rejected") and advisory_constraints (failed checks are recorded in ModelResult.advisory_violations without changing the error). check_constraints(expr) runs the pre-checks without evaluating, billing or recording anything, and returns the failed required and advisory checks as two lists. max_constants / max_expr_length add a MaxConstants / MaxTokens in front of the list unless it already has one.
  • Background knowledge on datasets (SRToolkit.dataset.background_knowledge): BackgroundKnowledge holds what a task tells the approach besides the data (symbol library, samplers, constant bounds, advisory constraints, a reference grammar, task/variable/target descriptions as VariableInfo), without the answer. SR_dataset, from_samplers, SR_benchmark.add_dataset and add_from_samplers take its parts as arguments (variables=, target=, description=, advisory_constraints=, reference_grammar=, …) and expose it as dataset.background_knowledge. Its advisory constraints are stored set up on its symbol library, so their checks can run. dataset.describe() renders it for people and LLM prompts without the ground truth.
  • SR_dataset takes required_constraints, and max_constants / max_expr_length are named parameters that become MaxConstants / MaxTokens in that list. create_evaluator passes the required constraints and the background knowledge's advisory ones to the evaluator. constant_bounds is a named parameter too and goes into the background knowledge. dataset.ranking_settings() returns the settings the ranking gets (pass them to HoldoutMetric to score held-out data under the search's settings).
  • Samplers can be given as a mapping {token: sampler}.
  • Expression constraints describe themselves: describe() gives a short phrase (e.g. "at most 8 free constants") and summary() a plain record (e.g. {"kind": "max_constants", "limit": 8}). BackgroundKnowledge.priors() and SR_dataset.priors() list the records of the advisory (and required) constraints, and describe() uses the phrases. Samplers describe themselves too (UniformSampling(1, 5).describe() is "uniform on [-5, -1] ∪ [1, 5]").
  • Approaches can read the task during a run: SR_evaluator takes variables=, target=, description= and reference_grammar=, builds background_knowledge from them, the symbol library, the advisory constraints and the constant_bounds / samplers settings, and has describe() and priors(), equal to the dataset's for an evaluator from create_evaluator. SR_dataset.required_constraints are stored set up on the dataset's symbol library, so approaches can run their checks.
  • ProGED without a grammar samples from the dataset's reference_grammar when it has one (logged at INFO), else from a generic grammar. A ProGED instance reused on another dataset no longer keeps the first dataset's grammar.
  • ProGED skips samples it already evaluated or that break a required constraint, so its budget goes to new valid expressions; after max_consecutive_skips (default 10000) skips in a row it stops early with a warning. skip_evaluated=False / skip_rejected=False turn either kind of skipping off.
  • EDHiE trains its HVAE on expressions from the dataset's reference_grammar when it has one (logged at INFO), else from the symbol library, keeping only expressions that pass the required constraints (EDHiE.training_expressions returns them). Its search scores already evaluated individuals with their cached error and skips ones that break a required constraint, without using the budget, with the same skip_evaluated / skip_rejected / max_consecutive_skips settings as ProGED. A trained state can be shared only between datasets with the same symbol library, reference grammar and required constraints. training_seed makes adapt reproducible and leaves the global random states as they were. EDHiE's adaptation_scope is now "never" only for a model given through weights_path; otherwise it stays "once", so an instance reused on another dataset trains for that dataset instead of keeping the first model.
  • BackgroundKnowledge.reference_grammar must use only symbols of the symbol library, brackets and numbers (ValueError otherwise; Grammar.unknown_tokens(symbol_library) lists the offending tokens), and BackgroundKnowledge.sampling_grammar() returns the grammar approaches sample from: the reference grammar, else a generic grammar for the library.
  • SR_evaluator.get_model(expr) returns the result of an already evaluated expression, or None, without using the budget.
  • evaluate_approach now calls prepare() before a "once" adaptation, as the docs say and ExperimentJob.run already did. ExperimentGrid.adapt_one creates the parent directories of the state path, like the other adaptation paths.
  • SR_dataset.original_equation is derived when not given, from the ground truth with the variable and target names (e.g. F = m*a); only a given string is saved. SR_benchmark.list_datasets(verbose=True) shows it, also for datasets added with add_dataset_instance (previously None).
  • Feynman and SRSD datasets carry a name and description for every variable and the target, and a task description. SRSD equations are now derived from these names.

Breaking changes: - Removed the RMSE, BED and R2 augmenters; use HoldoutMetric. - EstimationSettings is renamed to RankingSettings. - Removed the bed_X and domain_bounds settings; pass the points as X with num_points_sampled=-1, or give samplers. - ground_truth must be an expression (token list or Node); a precomputed behavior matrix goes in the bed_gt setting. - Removed SR_evaluator.to_dict / from_dict; serialise the dataset instead. - Datasets are saved with format_version: 3; loading format_version: 1 configs is no longer supported (version 2 still loads). - EvalResult stores all_models (in first-seen order), trace, success_threshold and top_k; min_error, best_expr, success, num_evaluated and evaluation_calls are now read-only properties derived from them, so the constructor no longer takes them. top_models is now a method, top_models(k=None), returning the k best models (default top_k); it returns the same objects as all_models, breaks ties in error by expression length (shorter first) and then by first-seen order, and is no longer written to JSON. Results are saved with format_version: 2; results saved by earlier versions cannot be loaded and raise a ValueError saying so. - SR_evaluator.models is a list in first-seen order instead of a dict keyed by the expression string, and total_evaluations is a read-only property (len(trace)). - Calls to evaluate_expr after evaluation has stopped are no longer counted in total_evaluations / evaluation_calls. - The module-level sampling helpers in SRToolkit.dataset.sampling (uniform_sampling, log_uniform_sampling, …) are now private; use the UniformSampling, LogUniformSampling and IntegerUniformSampling classes. - Regression metrics (mse, rmse, mae, r2, nrmse) raise a ValueError unless predict(X) and y are 1-D of length len(X). Previously a (n, 1) target was silently broadcast against (n,) predictions into an (n, n) array, giving a meaningless value. - r2 and nrmse with constant targets return 1.0 / 0.0 for an exact prediction and -inf / inf otherwise, instead of nan. predict is now always called, so its exceptions propagate. - REGRESSION_METRICS is a read-only mapping. - SR_approach.adapt(X, symbol_library) is now adapt(X, background_knowledge, required_constraints); the symbol library is background_knowledge.symbol_library. Adapted states cached with adaptation_scope="once" were built from the old input and are reused as is; delete them (or adapt_one(..., force=True)) to re-adapt. - save_adapted_state / load_adapted_state must use exactly path: the framework restores a state only if that file exists. - tokens_to_tree, compile_expr and compile_expr_rmse raise a TypeError for an expression that is not a list of token strings or a Node (previously a bare Exception, or numpy's "expected str instance" message). Numbers in token lists must be strings ("1.5"); passing 1.5 now says so. - Invalid arguments to edit_distance, tree_edit_distance, create_behavior_matrix and bed raise TypeError or ValueError naming the offending parameter, instead of a bare Exception, UnboundLocalError or AttributeError (a string or tuple passed to edit_distance used to be compared character by character). bed and create_behavior_matrix now validate num_consts_sampled, consts_bounds, num_points_sampled, matrix shapes and the row counts of matrices against X. - Values that cannot be saved as JSON (complex numbers, datetime64, sets, masked arrays, arbitrary objects) in augmentations, ranking data or approach configs now raise a TypeError from to_dict naming the value's location (for results the full path, e.g. all_models[3].ranking_data['z']), instead of failing later in json.dump. Saved arrays now include dtype and shape, and tuples and non-string-keyed dicts are written in a new form, so files saved by this version cannot be read by earlier versions. - ModelResult.from_dict raises a ValueError for a status that is not one of STATUSES, instead of failing later in status_counts with a KeyError. - The grammar base class Constraint is renamed GrammarConstraint. - The status_detail of a rejected expression names the constraint, e.g. "MaxConstants: 9 constants, limit 8" instead of "9 constants exceed max_constants=8". - max_constants / max_expr_length must be ints (numpy ints accepted); other values raise a ValueError instead of being silently ignored. Giving one together with a required constraint of the same class and a different limit raises a ValueError; a negative setting adds no limit and never clashes. - Datasets are saved with format_version: 4 (symbol library and samplers inside "background_knowledge", limits in "required_constraints"). Files of format 2 and 3 still load, and their data cache stays valid. SR_dataset.symbol_library, samplers and constant_bounds are read-only, samplers is a tuple, and kwargs no longer contains constant_bounds, max_constants or max_expr_length. A sampler count that differs from the number of variables now raises a ValueError. - SR_benchmark.add_dataset raises a ValueError (instead of Exception) when the ground truth cannot be evaluated, and a ValueError when neither dataset nor data_source is given (such an entry could never be loaded). - SR_dataset.original_equation is a read-only property.

Fixes: - HoldoutMetric no longer applies the estimator's default limit of 8 constants when fitting constants on held-out data: max_constants / max_expr_length apply only if given in ranking_settings. Before, a model the search accepted (e.g. under a required MaxConstants(20)) got NaN on the holdout. - HoldoutMetric with a RankingFunction metric gives NaN to models the search did not score "ok", like the built-in and callable metrics already did. Before, it scored rejected models on the held-out data, so they could look like valid answers. - A dataset with custom constant_bounds scored every expression with a constant as NaN after a JSON round trip (from_dict, from_archive, ExperimentGrid). - A Node ground truth is now serialised with the dataset's own symbol library. - SR_dataset.refresh() regenerates the test and aux data too, and data_cache.remove deletes them. - Saving results no longer fails on dict keys that are numpy scalars (e.g. np.int64) or on object arrays holding arrays. - SR_dataset now describes BED datasets correctly. - Compiled expressions given fewer constants than they use raise a ValueError on every backend. The default "stack" backend used to read past the end of the array and return garbage values. A SampleSource whose ground truth has a free constant (C) now fails with a clear error, as SR_dataset.resample already did, instead of generating a dataset with garbage y; the custom-dataset guide example that used one is fixed (#4). - EvalResult saves metadata like its other fields, so tuples, numpy arrays and numpy scalars in it round-trip exactly; previously a numpy value made json.dump fail and tuples came back as lists. A numpy wall_time no longer breaks saving either. - add_augmentation (on ModelResult and EvalResult) stores a shallow copy of data and no longer adds "_type" to the caller's dict. - EvalResult.calls_to_threshold ignores models with a non-finite error, like the other trace metrics. - Augmenters with scope="all" annotated the top models twice (e.g. ExpressionToLatex and ExpressionToLatex_1). - Fixed examples in the benchmarking, grammars, quickstart and experiments guides and the README (a wrong benchmark, a derivation that never finished, inconsistent file names) (#5). - bed gave wrong values when called with two behavior matrices that have different numbers of columns, e.g. a ground-truth matrix sampled with a different num_consts_sampled. BEDRanking always compares matrices of equal width, so rankings were not affected. - bed returned 0 for points where one expression is nan and the other infinite, or where they are +inf and -inf. Such points now give inf; points where both expressions are the same infinity give 0, as documented. - Evaluating an expression on an X with too few columns (or a 1-D X) read past the end of the array on the default "stack" backend and returned garbage; it now raises a ValueError. This affected compile_expr, create_behavior_matrix and bed. - tree_edit_distance priced relabelling by the character edit distance between symbols when the optional editdistance package was installed, so results depended on the environment. It now always uses unit costs. - Regression metrics no longer emit NumPy warnings on empty or non-finite input; the returned nan / inf is the signal. - MaxOccurrences let a grammar rule containing the symbol several times (e.g. E -> x * x) exceed the limit. - SR_benchmark.create_dataset no longer turns every error from loading an entry into a bare ValueError: TypeError, ImportError and FileNotFoundError pass through, and a ValueError keeps its cause. - SR_dataset and SR_benchmark.add_dataset raise a ValueError when the data's number of columns differs from the number of variables in the symbol library. Such a dataset was accepted before and failed or misbehaved later (e.g. list_datasets(num_variables=...) missed it, resampling drew the wrong number of columns). - SR_benchmark.from_dict no longer modifies the dict it is given. - SR_dataset.evaluate_approach seeds experiment i with initial_seed + i (or the dataset seed + i), like ExperimentGrid does. It used + i + 1, so the given seed itself was never used; runs with the same initial_seed now give different results than before (use initial_seed + 1 to reproduce them). - is_float returns False for values float cannot convert (lists, complex numbers, arbitrary objects) instead of raising a TypeError. - An SR_evaluator whose required constraints allow more than 8 free constants no longer has its parameter estimator reject such expressions at its default limit of 8. - SRSD Bonus 6: the ground truth used epsilon instead of epsilon**2. Fixed together with its data (SRSD data version 1.0.1); its targets no longer contain NaN.

docs.title: SymbolicRegressionToolkit-1.6.0 (2026-06-23)
docs.text:
• New backends for expression evaluations (about 1.5x speedup for parameter estimation)
  • SymbolLibrary can now be as a global default or used with the ContextManager (with SymbolLibrary()...:)
  • Added grammars (CFG, PCFG) and the ability to add constraints to them.
  • Added a TimeLimitCallback
  • Added wallclock time to experiment
  • Added some default constraints that work as built-ins and reference implementations
  • Added guides to the documentation
  • Added some tests
  • Reworked how sharing code/benchmark works:
  • Code is shared through bundles, which can be installed and are directly usable after
  • Datasets/benchmarks are versioned and can be shared via .zip files, of through configs implementing DataSources
  • Configs should be shared directly and should be run through pack, so they are directly usable
  • ExperimentGrid can now be exported together with all the bundles and data it needs. Custom code is shipped only via re-packed installed bundles or explicit .srtk files passed to export(additional_bundles=...) (no more guessing a bundle from a loose source file); uncovered classes warn, or raise with export(strict=True)

docs.title: SymbolicRegressionToolkit-1.5.0 (2026-04-14)
docs.text:
• Reworked how SR_results and ResultAugmenters work
  • Improved documentation
  • Fixed some bugs
  • Made the interface more consistent and easier to use
  • Two instances of SR_benchmarks are now in separate files and allow resampling of data
  • All (or at least all relevant) classes can now be saved and loaded/transformed into and from a dictionary
  • Added some tests (a lot more to go)
  • Added new examples

New Features:

  • Added a base class for approaches and implemented ProGED and EDHiE
  • Added a way to run generate and run experiments easily
  • Added the callback system to allow custom events during experiments
