    self,
    ground_truth: Union[List[str], Node],
    samplers: Optional[Union[List[Sampler], Mapping[str, Sampler]]] = None,
    symbol_library: Optional[SymbolLibrary] = None,
    n_samples: int = 10000,
    seed: Optional[int] = None,
    ranking_function: str = "rmse",
    dataset_name: Optional[str] = None,
    original_equation: Optional[str] = None,
    success_threshold: Optional[float] = None,
    max_evaluations: int = -1,
    dataset_metadata: Optional[dict] = None,
    variables: Optional[Mapping[str, VariableInfo]] = None,
    target: Optional[VariableInfo] = None,
    description: Optional[str] = None,
    constant_bounds: Optional[Tuple[float, float]] = None,
    reference_grammar: Optional[Grammar] = None,
    max_constants: Optional[int] = None,
    max_expr_length: Optional[int] = None,
    required_constraints: Optional[Iterable[ExpressionConstraint]] = None,
    advisory_constraints: Optional[Iterable[ExpressionConstraint]] = None,
    **kwargs: Unpack[RankingSettings],
) -> None:
    """Add a dataset described by a ground-truth expression and per-variable samplers.

    The benchmark-level counterpart to
    [SR_dataset.from_samplers][SRToolkit.dataset.sr_dataset.SR_dataset.from_samplers]: it
    attaches a [SampleSource][SRToolkit.dataset.data_source.SampleSource], so the data is
    generated lazily from the samplers (and, for RMSE, ``ground_truth``) the first time the
    dataset is materialised via
    [create_dataset][SRToolkit.dataset.sr_benchmark.SR_benchmark.create_dataset]. Nothing is
    written to the data cache here.

    Args:
        ground_truth: Ground-truth expression as a token list or
            [Node][SRToolkit.utils.expression_tree.Node].
        samplers: One [Sampler][SRToolkit.dataset.sampling.Sampler] per variable, as a list
            in the library's variable order or a mapping ``{token: sampler}``.
        symbol_library: Token vocabulary. ``None`` uses
            [default_symbols][SRToolkit.utils.symbol_library.SymbolLibrary.default_symbols]
            with one variable per sampler.
        n_samples: Number of input rows to generate on materialisation. Defaults to ``10000``.
        seed: Random seed stored on the
            [SampleSource][SRToolkit.dataset.data_source.SampleSource].
        ranking_function: ``"rmse"`` or ``"bed"``.
        dataset_name: Name of the dataset. Auto-generated if ``None``.
        original_equation: As for
            [add_dataset][SRToolkit.dataset.sr_benchmark.SR_benchmark.add_dataset].
        success_threshold: Error threshold for success. ``None`` means no threshold.
        max_evaluations: Maximum expressions to evaluate. ``-1`` means no limit.
        dataset_metadata: Optional dataset-level metadata dict.
        variables: Information per variable, as for
            [SR_dataset][SRToolkit.dataset.sr_dataset.SR_dataset].
        target: Information about the target, as for ``SR_dataset``.
        description: Free text about the task, as for ``SR_dataset``.
        constant_bounds: Range free constants are fitted in, as for ``SR_dataset``.
        reference_grammar: A grammar an approach may start from, as for ``SR_dataset``.
        max_constants: Free-constant limit, as for ``SR_dataset`` (``None``: 8).
        max_expr_length: Token limit, as for ``SR_dataset`` (``None``: no limit).
        required_constraints: Further required constraints, as for ``SR_dataset``.
        advisory_constraints: Hints about the search space, as for ``SR_dataset``.
        **kwargs: Ranking settings, as for ``SR_dataset``.

    Raises:
        ValueError: If ``samplers`` is ``None`` or empty, or as for
            [add_dataset][SRToolkit.dataset.sr_benchmark.SR_benchmark.add_dataset].
        TypeError: As for ``add_dataset``.

    Examples:
        >>> from SRToolkit.dataset.sampling import UniformSampling
        >>> bm = SR_benchmark("BM")
        >>> bm.add_from_samplers(["X_0", "+", "X_1"],
        ...     [UniformSampling(0, 5), UniformSampling(0, 5)], dataset_name="add",
        ...     n_samples=100, seed=0)
        >>> ds = bm.create_dataset("add")
        >>> ds.X.shape
        (100, 2)
    """
    if not samplers:
        raise ValueError(
            "[SR_benchmark.add_from_samplers] 'samplers' must be non-empty (one sampler per input variable)."
        )
    if symbol_library is None:
        symbol_library = SymbolLibrary.default_symbols(len(samplers))

    self.add_dataset(
        symbol_library=symbol_library,
        dataset=None,
        dataset_name=dataset_name,
        ranking_function=ranking_function,
        max_evaluations=max_evaluations,
        ground_truth=ground_truth,
        original_equation=original_equation,
        success_threshold=success_threshold,
        seed=seed,
        dataset_metadata=dataset_metadata,
        samplers=samplers,
        data_source=SampleSource(n_samples=n_samples, seed=seed),
        variables=variables,
        target=target,
        description=description,
        constant_bounds=constant_bounds,
        reference_grammar=reference_grammar,
        max_constants=max_constants,
        max_expr_length=max_expr_length,
        required_constraints=required_constraints,
        advisory_constraints=advisory_constraints,
        **kwargs,

def create_dataset(
    self,
    dataset_name: str,
    n_samples: Optional[int] = None,
    seed: Optional[int] = None,
) -> SR_dataset:
    """Creates an instance of a dataset from the given dataset name.

    When ``n_samples`` is provided the returned dataset contains freshly sampled data
    instead of the pre-generated data on disk. The dataset must have samplers defined
    (see ``samplers`` argument of
    [add_dataset][SRToolkit.dataset.sr_benchmark.SR_benchmark.add_dataset]). Entries of format
    2 or 3 from older saved benchmarks are migrated as by
    [SR_dataset.from_dict][SRToolkit.dataset.sr_dataset.SR_dataset.from_dict].

    Examples:
        >>> from SRToolkit.dataset import Feynman
        >>> benchmark = Feynman() # Feynman is a specific instance of SR_benchmark with additional functionality
        >>> dataset = benchmark.create_dataset('I.16.6')
        >>> dataset.X.shape
        (10000, 3)
        >>> dataset_small = benchmark.create_dataset('I.16.6', n_samples=500, seed=0)
        >>> dataset_small.X.shape
        (500, 3)

    Args:
        dataset_name: The name of the dataset to create.
        n_samples: If provided, generate a fresh dataset with this many samples using
            the stored samplers instead of loading pre-generated data from disk.
        seed: Random seed used when ``n_samples`` is provided. If ``None``, no seed is set.

    Returns:
        An [SR_dataset][SRToolkit.dataset.sr_dataset.SR_dataset] instance containing the
        data, ground truth expression, and metadata for the given dataset.

    Raises:
        ValueError: If the dataset name is not found; ``n_samples`` is provided but the
            dataset has no samplers defined; or ``SR_dataset.from_dict`` raises a ``ValueError``
            for the entry (raised from it, with the dataset name).
        TypeError: As for ``SR_dataset.from_dict``, unchanged.
        ImportError: As for ``SR_dataset.from_dict``, unchanged.
        FileNotFoundError: As for ``SR_dataset.from_dict``, unchanged.
    """
    if dataset_name not in self.datasets:
        raise ValueError(f"Dataset {dataset_name} not found")

    if n_samples is not None:
        config = self.datasets[dataset_name]
        if _config_samplers(config) is None:
            raise ValueError(
                f"[SR_benchmark.create_dataset] Cannot resample '{dataset_name}': no samplers defined."
            )
        # _create_from_entry may return the benchmark's stored SR_dataset instance
        # (for entries added via add_dataset_instance). Copy before mutating X/y so
        # resampling never corrupts the stored dataset or aliases across callers.
        dataset = copy.deepcopy(self._create_from_entry(config))
        return dataset.resample_inplace(n_samples, seed=seed)

    # Loading canonical data: materialisation is driven entirely by each dataset's
    # ``data_source`` — the built-ins use a FallbackSource that downloads the canonical
    # archive once and regenerates from samplers only if the download is unavailable.
    return self._create_from_entry(self.datasets[dataset_name])

def list_datasets(self, verbose: bool = True, num_variables: int = -1) -> List[str]:
    """Return the names of the datasets, optionally printing a line per dataset.

    Nothing is built. With ``verbose``, each line gives the name, the number of variables and
    the equation: the entry's ``original_equation``, or derived as for
    [SR_dataset.original_equation][SRToolkit.dataset.sr_dataset.SR_dataset.original_equation]
    when not given (for an entry added with ``add_dataset_instance``, that dataset's
    ``original_equation``). An entry without an equation shows only its name and number of
    variables.

    Args:
        verbose: If ``True``, print one line per dataset.
        num_variables: If not ``-1``, only return datasets with this many input variables.

    Returns:
        The dataset names, sorted by number of variables, then by name.

    Examples:
        >>> from SRToolkit.dataset import Feynman
        >>> benchmark = Feynman() # Feynman is a specific instance of SR_benchmark with additional functionality
        >>> len(benchmark.list_datasets(num_variables=2, verbose=False))
        15
        >>> datasets_with_8_vars = benchmark.list_datasets(num_variables=8, verbose=False)
        >>> datasets_with_8_vars[0]
        'II.36.38'
    """
    datasets = [
        dataset_name
        for dataset_name in self.datasets
        if num_variables < 0 or self.datasets[dataset_name].get("num_variables") == num_variables
    ]
    datasets = sorted(
        datasets,
        key=lambda dataset_name: (
            self.datasets[dataset_name].get("num_variables", -1),
            dataset_name,
        ),
    )

    if verbose:
        part1 = []
        part2 = []
        part3 = []
        max_length_1 = 0
        max_length_2 = 0
        for d in datasets:
            nv = self.datasets[d].get("num_variables", -1)
            if nv == 1:
                variable_str = "1 variable"
            elif nv is None or nv < 1:
                variable_str = "Amount of variables unknown"
            else:
                variable_str = f"{nv} variables"
            part1.append(d + ":")
            part2.append(variable_str)
            entry = self.datasets[d]
            if "sr_dataset" in entry:
                equation = entry["sr_dataset"].original_equation
            elif entry.get("original_equation") is not None or entry.get("ground_truth") is None:
                equation = entry.get("original_equation")
            else:
                bk = entry.get("background_knowledge") or {}
                target = bk.get("target")
                equation = _derive_equation(
                    entry["ground_truth"],
                    {k: VariableInfo.from_dict(v) for k, v in (bk.get("variables") or {}).items()},
                    VariableInfo.from_dict(target) if target is not None else None,
                )
            part3.append(equation)
            if len(d) + 1 > max_length_1:
                max_length_1 = len(d) + 1
            if len(variable_str) > max_length_2:
                max_length_2 = len(variable_str)

        for p1, p2, p3 in zip(part1, part2, part3):
            line = f"{p1:<{max_length_1}} {p2:<{max_length_2}}"
            print(line if p3 is None else f"{line}, Expression: {p3}")
    return datasets

def to_dict(self) -> dict:
    """Serialise the benchmark to a pure JSON-safe dictionary.

    Dataset entries that have an ``sr_dataset`` key (added via
    [add_dataset_instance][SRToolkit.dataset.sr_benchmark.SR_benchmark.add_dataset_instance])
    are serialised via ``SR_dataset.to_dict()``.

    Returns:
        A JSON-safe dict representing the full benchmark configuration.
    """
    datasets_out = {}
    for name, entry in self.datasets.items():
        if "sr_dataset" in entry:
            datasets_out[name] = entry["sr_dataset"].to_dict()
        else:
            datasets_out[name] = {k: v for k, v in entry.items() if k != "sr_dataset"}

    return {
        "format_version": 2,
        "type": "SR_benchmark",
        "benchmark_name": self.benchmark_name,
        "version": self.version,
        "metadata": self.metadata,
        "datasets": datasets_out,
    }

@classmethod
def from_dict(cls, d: Union[dict, str, Path]) -> "SR_benchmark":
    """Reconstruct an SR_benchmark from a config dict or a saved JSON file.

    To load a self-contained ``.zip`` archive (written by
    [to_archive][SRToolkit.dataset.sr_benchmark.SR_benchmark.to_archive]) use
    [from_archive][SRToolkit.dataset.sr_benchmark.SR_benchmark.from_archive] instead.
    Dataset entries of format 2 or 3 in older files are accepted and migrated as by
    [SR_dataset.from_dict][SRToolkit.dataset.sr_dataset.SR_dataset.from_dict]. The entries are
    copied, so ``d`` is not changed.

    Args:
        d: A dict produced by [to_dict][SRToolkit.dataset.sr_benchmark.SR_benchmark.to_dict],
            or a path to a JSON file.

    Returns:
        An [SR_benchmark][SRToolkit.dataset.sr_benchmark.SR_benchmark] instance.
    """
    if isinstance(d, (str, Path)):
        if str(d).endswith(".zip"):
            raise ValueError(
                "[SR_benchmark.from_dict] Received a '.zip' path. Load self-contained "
                "archives with SR_benchmark.from_archive(path) instead."
            )
        with open(d) as f:
            dd = json.load(f)
    else:
        dd = d

    benchmark_name = dd["benchmark_name"]
    version = dd.get("version", "1.0.0")
    metadata = dd.get("metadata", {})

    b = cls(benchmark_name, version=version, metadata=metadata)

    for name, entry in dd.get("datasets", {}).items():
        # Store a copy of the entry (the caller's dict is not changed); materialisation is lazy
        # via create_dataset.
        entry = copy.deepcopy(entry)
        b.datasets[name] = entry
        if "num_variables" not in entry:
            # Try to infer
            samplers = _config_samplers(entry)
            if samplers is not None:
                entry["num_variables"] = len(samplers)
            else:
                entry["num_variables"] = -1

    return b

def to_archive(self, path: Union[str, Path]) -> None:
    """Write the benchmark (config + data) to a ``.zip`` archive.

    The archive contains:

    - ``benchmark.json``: the benchmark configuration dict.
    - ``data/<dataset_name>.npz``: the cached data for each dataset.

    Args:
        path: Destination path for the archive.  Non-``.zip`` suffixes trigger a
            warning but are still accepted.
    """
    path = Path(path)
    if path.suffix.lower() != ".zip":
        warnings.warn(
            f"[SR_benchmark.to_archive] path '{path}' does not end in '.zip'. "
            "The file will be a ZIP archive regardless of the extension.",
            stacklevel=2,
        )

    benchmark_json = json.dumps(self.to_dict(), indent=2)

    with zipfile.ZipFile(str(path), "w", compression=zipfile.ZIP_DEFLATED) as zf:
        zf.writestr("benchmark.json", benchmark_json)

        for name, entry in self.datasets.items():
            if "sr_dataset" in entry:
                # In-memory dataset — write its data
                ds = entry["sr_dataset"]
                cache_p = data_cache.dataset_path(self.benchmark_name, self.version, name)
                if not cache_p.exists():
                    # Write directly from arrays
                    buf = io.BytesIO()
                    if ds.y is not None:
                        np.savez(buf, X=ds.X, y=ds.y)
                    else:
                        np.savez(buf, X=ds.X)
                    zf.writestr(f"data/{name}.npz", buf.getvalue())
                    continue
            else:
                ds_name = entry.get("dataset_name", name)
                try:
                    cache_p = data_cache.resolve(self.benchmark_name, self.version, ds_name, entry)
                except Exception as e:
                    warnings.warn(f"[SR_benchmark.to_archive] Could not materialise '{name}': {e}. Skipping.")
                    continue

            zf.write(str(cache_p), f"data/{name}.npz")

@classmethod
def from_archive(cls, path: Union[str, Path]) -> "SR_benchmark":
    """Load a benchmark from a self-contained ``.zip`` archive.

    This is the counterpart to
    [to_archive][SRToolkit.dataset.sr_benchmark.SR_benchmark.to_archive]: it reads
    ``benchmark.json`` from the archive, extracts the bundled ``data/*.npz`` into the data
    cache, and returns a benchmark whose datasets read from that populated cache.

    Args:
        path: Path to a ``.zip`` archive written by
            [to_archive][SRToolkit.dataset.sr_benchmark.SR_benchmark.to_archive].

    Returns:
        An [SR_benchmark][SRToolkit.dataset.sr_benchmark.SR_benchmark] instance.
    """
    with zipfile.ZipFile(str(path), "r") as zf:
        benchmark_dict = json.loads(zf.read("benchmark.json"))

    benchmark_name = benchmark_dict["benchmark_name"]
    version = benchmark_dict.get("version", "1.0.0")

    # Extract data into the cache
    data_cache.import_archive(Path(path), benchmark_name, version)

    b = cls(benchmark_name, version=version, metadata=benchmark_dict.get("metadata", {}))
    for name, entry in benchmark_dict.get("datasets", {}).items():
        b.datasets[name] = entry
        if "num_variables" not in entry:
            entry["num_variables"] = -1

    return b

@classmethod
def from_url(cls, url: str) -> "SR_benchmark":
    """Download a self-contained ``.zip`` archive from a URL and load it.

    This is the remote counterpart to
    [from_archive][SRToolkit.dataset.sr_benchmark.SR_benchmark.from_archive]: the
    archive is downloaded to a temporary file and then loaded exactly as
    ``from_archive`` would. The ``url`` must point at an archive written by
    [to_archive][SRToolkit.dataset.sr_benchmark.SR_benchmark.to_archive] (a
    ``benchmark.json`` plus a ``data/`` directory) — not a bare ``.npz``/data zip
    (that is what [UrlSource][SRToolkit.dataset.data_source.UrlSource] is for).

    Args:
        url: URL of a ``.zip`` archive written by
            [to_archive][SRToolkit.dataset.sr_benchmark.SR_benchmark.to_archive].

    Returns:
        An [SR_benchmark][SRToolkit.dataset.sr_benchmark.SR_benchmark] instance.
    """
    with urlopen(url) as response:
        data = response.read()

    tmp = tempfile.NamedTemporaryFile(suffix=".zip", delete=False)
    try:
        tmp.write(data)
        tmp.close()
        return cls.from_archive(tmp.name)
    finally:
        os.unlink(tmp.name)

def __init__(  # type: ignore[misc]
    self,
    X: np.ndarray,
    symbol_library: SymbolLibrary,
    ranking_function: str = "rmse",
    y: Optional[np.ndarray] = None,
    max_evaluations: int = -1,
    ground_truth: Optional[Union[List[str], Node]] = None,
    original_equation: Optional[str] = None,
    success_threshold: Optional[float] = None,
    seed: Optional[int] = None,
    dataset_metadata: Optional[dict] = None,
    dataset_name: str = "unnamed",
    samplers: Optional[Union[List[Sampler], Mapping[str, Sampler]]] = None,
    benchmark: Optional[str] = None,
    version: Optional[str] = None,
    test_X: Optional[np.ndarray] = None,
    test_y: Optional[np.ndarray] = None,
    aux_data: Optional[Dict[str, Union[Dict[str, np.ndarray], DataSplit]]] = None,
    variables: Optional[Mapping[str, VariableInfo]] = None,
    target: Optional[VariableInfo] = None,
    description: Optional[str] = None,
    constant_bounds: Optional[Tuple[float, float]] = None,
    reference_grammar: Optional[Grammar] = None,
    max_constants: Optional[int] = None,
    max_expr_length: Optional[int] = None,
    required_constraints: Optional[Iterable[ExpressionConstraint]] = None,
    advisory_constraints: Optional[Iterable[ExpressionConstraint]] = None,
    **kwargs: Unpack[RankingSettings],
) -> None:
    self._background_knowledge, self._required_constraints, kwargs = _resolve_task(  # type: ignore[assignment]
        {
            "symbol_library": symbol_library,
            "samplers": samplers,
            "variables": variables,
            "target": target,
            "description": description,
            "constant_bounds": constant_bounds,
            "reference_grammar": reference_grammar,
            "constraints": advisory_constraints,
        },
        max_constants,
        max_expr_length,
        required_constraints,
        kwargs,
        X,
    )

    self.max_evaluations = max_evaluations
    self.success_threshold = success_threshold
    self.ranking_function = ranking_function
    if isinstance(ground_truth, np.ndarray):
        raise ValueError(
            "[SR_dataset] An ndarray ground_truth (a precomputed BED behaviour matrix) is no longer "
            "supported on SR_dataset; provide a symbolic ground truth (a token list or a Node). A "
            "precomputed behaviour matrix is ranking-owned state — pass it to the BED ranking instead."
        )
    self.ground_truth = ground_truth
    self._original_equation = original_equation
    self.kwargs = kwargs
    self.dataset_name = dataset_name

    # The data lives in DataSplits: the train split (X / y, the data the search runs on), an
    # optional held-out test split, and optional extra splits for the user's own measures.
    train_arrays: Dict[str, np.ndarray] = {"X": X}
    if y is not None:
        train_arrays["y"] = y
    self._train = DataSplit(train_arrays)
    self.test: Optional[DataSplit] = None
    if test_X is not None:
        test_arrays: Dict[str, np.ndarray] = {"X": test_X}
        if test_y is not None:
            test_arrays["y"] = test_y
        self.test = DataSplit(test_arrays)
    self.aux_data: Dict[str, DataSplit] = {}
    for key, value in (aux_data or {}).items():
        self._validate_aux_key(key)
        self.aux_data[key] = value if isinstance(value, DataSplit) else DataSplit(dict(value))

    # See if symbols contain a symbol for constants
    symbols_metadata = self.symbol_library.symbols.values()
    self.contains_constants = any([symbol["type"] == "const" for symbol in symbols_metadata])

    self.seed = seed
    self.dataset_metadata = dataset_metadata

    # Cache / serialisation metadata
    self.benchmark = benchmark
    self.version = version
    # Origin of the cached data (UrlSource / SampleSource / None). Not a constructor
    # argument: it is set by the factory methods (from_dict, from_samplers) and by
    # SR_benchmark.add_dataset. End users select an origin through those entry points.
    # data_source is a view over the train split's source (see the property below).
    self.data_source = None

def evaluate_approach(
    self,
    sr_approach: SR_approach,
    num_experiments: int = 1,
    top_k: int = 20,
    initial_seed: Optional[int] = None,
    results: Optional[SR_results] = None,
    callbacks: Optional[Union[SRCallbacks, CallbackDispatcher, List[SRCallbacks]]] = None,
    verbose: bool = True,
    adaptation_path: Optional[str] = None,
) -> SR_results:
    """Run an SR approach on this dataset and collect the results.

    Each experiment searches with a new evaluator from
    [create_evaluator][SRToolkit.dataset.sr_dataset.SR_dataset.create_evaluator]. Experiment ``i``
    (from 0) is seeded with ``seed + i``, where ``seed`` is ``initial_seed`` or the dataset seed; it
    is unseeded if both are ``None``. Approaches with ``adaptation_scope="once"`` adapt before the
    first experiment, those with ``"experiment"`` before each one;
    [adapt][SRToolkit.approaches.sr_approach.SR_approach.adapt] gets ``X``, ``background_knowledge``
    and ``required_constraints``.

    Args:
        sr_approach: The approach to run.
        num_experiments: Number of independent runs.
        top_k: Number of best expressions kept per run.
        initial_seed: Base seed; ``None`` uses the dataset seed.
        results: [SR_results][SRToolkit.evaluation.sr_evaluator.SR_results] to append to in place;
            ``None`` creates a new one.
        callbacks: An [SRCallbacks][SRToolkit.evaluation.callbacks.SRCallbacks], a list of them, or a
            [CallbackDispatcher][SRToolkit.evaluation.callbacks.CallbackDispatcher].
        verbose: Print a line as each experiment starts.
        adaptation_path: For ``adaptation_scope="once"``: load the adapted state from this file if it
            exists, otherwise adapt and save it there, creating its parent directories. ``None``
            adapts without saving.

    Returns:
        ``results`` (or a new ``SR_results``) with one entry per experiment.

    Examples:
        >>> results = dataset.evaluate_approach(my_approach, num_experiments=5)  # doctest: +SKIP
    """
    base_seed = self.seed if initial_seed is None else initial_seed

    if results is None:
        results = SR_results()

    if isinstance(callbacks, SRCallbacks):
        dispatcher = CallbackDispatcher(callbacks=[callbacks])
        callbacks = dispatcher
    elif isinstance(callbacks, list):
        if len(callbacks) == 0:
            callbacks = None
        else:
            callbacks = CallbackDispatcher(callbacks=callbacks)

    dataset_name = self.dataset_name

    for experiment in range(num_experiments):
        if verbose:
            print(f"Running experiment {experiment + 1}/{num_experiments}")
        # Experiment i gets base_seed + i, as job i of an ExperimentGrid does.
        seed = None if base_seed is None else base_seed + experiment

        event = ExperimentEvent(
            dataset_name=dataset_name,
            approach_name=sr_approach.name,
            success_threshold=self.success_threshold,
            max_evaluations=self.max_evaluations,
            seed=seed,
        )
        if callbacks is not None:
            callbacks.on_experiment_start(event)

        sr_approach.prepare()

        if sr_approach.adaptation_scope == "once" and experiment == 0:
            if adaptation_path is not None and os.path.exists(adaptation_path):
                sr_approach.load_adapted_state(adaptation_path)
            else:
                sr_approach.adapt(self.X, self.background_knowledge, self.required_constraints)
                if adaptation_path is not None:
                    dir_name = os.path.dirname(adaptation_path)
                    if dir_name:
                        os.makedirs(dir_name, exist_ok=True)
                    sr_approach.save_adapted_state(adaptation_path)
        elif sr_approach.adaptation_scope == "experiment":
            sr_approach.adapt(self.X, self.background_knowledge, self.required_constraints)

        evaluator = self.create_evaluator(seed=seed)
        evaluator._experiment_id = f"{dataset_name}_{sr_approach.name}_{seed}"
        evaluator.register_callbacks(callbacks)
        start_time = time.monotonic()
        sr_approach.search(evaluator, seed)
        elapsed = time.monotonic() - start_time
        experiment_results = evaluator.get_results(sr_approach.name, top_k)
        experiment_results.results[-1].wall_time = elapsed
        results += experiment_results

        if callbacks is not None:
            callbacks.on_experiment_end(event, results.results[-1])
    return results

def ranking_settings(self) -> Dict[str, Any]:
    """Return the settings the ranking function gets, as in an evaluator from ``create_evaluator``.

    They are ``kwargs`` plus ``constant_bounds``, plus ``samplers`` if the dataset has them
    (BED draws its points from them when it can; other rankings ignore them). Unless ``bed_resample``
    is set, ``ranking_seed`` defaults to the dataset seed (``0`` if ``None``), so every run is
    scored by the same objective. Pass them to
    [HoldoutMetric][SRToolkit.evaluation.result_augmentation.HoldoutMetric] to score held-out
    data under the search's settings.

    Returns:
        A new dict of settings; the limits ``max_constants`` / ``max_expr_length`` are not in it
        (they are in ``required_constraints``).
    """
    settings: Dict[str, Any] = dict(self.kwargs)
    settings["constant_bounds"] = self.constant_bounds
    if self.samplers is not None:
        settings["samplers"] = list(self.samplers)
    # Fix the ranking's randomness per dataset, unless the user asked for it to be resampled each run.
    if not settings.get("bed_resample", False):
        settings.setdefault("ranking_seed", self.seed if self.seed is not None else 0)
    return settings

def create_evaluator(self, metadata: Optional[Dict[str, Any]] = None, seed: Optional[int] = None) -> SR_evaluator:
    """Create an [SR_evaluator][SRToolkit.evaluation.sr_evaluator.SR_evaluator] for this dataset.

    The evaluator gets the parts of the background knowledge (its ``constraints`` as advisory
    constraints) and ``required_constraints`` as required, adds no limits of its own, and passes
    [ranking_settings][SRToolkit.dataset.sr_dataset.SR_dataset.ranking_settings] to the ranking.
    Its ``background_knowledge`` is rebuilt from these parts, so its ``to_dict()``,
    ``describe()`` and ``priors()`` equal this dataset's.

    Args:
        metadata: Metadata to attach to the evaluator; ``dataset_name`` and ``dataset_metadata`` are
            added to it in place.
        seed: Seed of the evaluator; ``None`` uses the dataset seed.

    Returns:
        The configured evaluator.

    Raises:
        ValueError: If the ranking rejects the dataset (e.g. RMSE with neither ``y`` nor
            ``ground_truth``).
        ImportError: If an import-path ``ranking_function`` cannot be imported.

    Examples:
        >>> X = np.array([[1, 2], [3, 4], [5, 6]])
        >>> dataset = SR_dataset(X, SymbolLibrary.default_symbols(2), y=np.array([3, 7, 11]))
        >>> float(dataset.create_evaluator().evaluate_expr(["X_1", "+", "X_0"]))  # doctest: +ELLIPSIS
        0.0...
    """
    if metadata is None:
        metadata = dict()
    if self.dataset_metadata is not None:
        metadata["dataset_metadata"] = self.dataset_metadata
    metadata["dataset_name"] = self.dataset_name

    return SR_evaluator(
        X=self.X,
        y=self.y,
        max_evaluations=self.max_evaluations,
        success_threshold=self.success_threshold,
        ranking_function=self.ranking_function,
        ground_truth=self.ground_truth,
        symbol_library=self.symbol_library,
        seed=self.seed if seed is None else seed,
        metadata=metadata,
        required_constraints=self.required_constraints,
        advisory_constraints=tuple(self.background_knowledge.constraints),
        variables=self.background_knowledge.variables,
        target=self.background_knowledge.target,
        description=self.background_knowledge.description,
        reference_grammar=self.background_knowledge.reference_grammar,
        # The limits are already in required_constraints; -1 adds none of the evaluator's own.
        max_constants=-1,
        max_expr_length=-1,
        **self.ranking_settings(),
    )

def __str__(self) -> str:
    """Return a description of the dataset, including the answer.

    It gives [original_equation][SRToolkit.dataset.sr_dataset.SR_dataset.original_equation] (omitted
    when ``None``), the ranking with its success rule and non-default settings, then
    [describe][SRToolkit.dataset.sr_dataset.SR_dataset.describe] and a pointer to
    ``dataset_metadata``. Use ``describe`` for prompts.

    Returns:
        The multi-line description.
    """
    equation = self.original_equation
    text = "" if equation is None else f"Dataset for target expression {equation}.\n"
    # Each ranking describes itself (and its success rule); no setup() is needed for that.
    text += build_ranking(self.ranking_function).describe(self.success_threshold)
    if not text.endswith("\n"):
        text += "\n"
    if self.kwargs:
        settings = ", ".join(f"{key}={value}" for key, value in self.kwargs.items())
        text += f"Non-default ranking settings: {settings}.\n"
    text += self.describe() + "\n"
    text += "For other metadata, please refer to the attribute self.dataset_metadata."
    return text

def resample(self, n: int, seed: Optional[int] = None) -> Union[np.ndarray, Tuple[np.ndarray, np.ndarray]]:
    """Draw new data from the samplers without changing the dataset.

    ``y`` is computed from ``ground_truth`` unless ``ranking_function`` is ``"bed"``.

    Args:
        n: Number of rows.
        seed: Seeds NumPy's global random state before the draw; ``None`` leaves it as is.

    Returns:
        ``X`` of shape ``(n, n_variables)`` if ``ranking_function`` is ``"bed"``, otherwise
        ``(X, y)`` with ``y`` of shape ``(n,)``.

    Raises:
        ValueError: If the dataset has no samplers, or ``y`` is needed and ``ground_truth`` is
            ``None`` or has a free constant.
    """
    if self.samplers is None:
        raise ValueError(
            f"[SR_dataset.resample] Dataset '{self.dataset_name}' has no samplers defined. "
            "Provide samplers when constructing the dataset."
        )
    if seed is not None:
        np.random.seed(seed)
    X = _sample_inputs(self.samplers, n)
    if self.ranking_function == "bed":
        return X
    if self.ground_truth is None or isinstance(self.ground_truth, np.ndarray):
        raise ValueError(
            f"[SR_dataset.resample] Dataset '{self.dataset_name}' has no token-list ground truth — "
            "cannot evaluate y. ground_truth must be a list of tokens or a Node."
        )

    _check_no_free_constants(
        self.ground_truth, self.symbol_library, f"[SR_dataset.resample] Dataset '{self.dataset_name}'"
    )

    f = compile_expr(self.ground_truth, self.symbol_library)
    y = f(X, np.array([]))
    return X, y

def resample_inplace(self, n: int, seed: Optional[int] = None) -> "SR_dataset":
    """Replace ``X`` and ``y`` with data from [resample][SRToolkit.dataset.sr_dataset.SR_dataset.resample].

def to_dict(self) -> dict:
    """Return a JSON-safe dictionary of this dataset's configuration (format 4).

    Arrays are not embedded but live in the [data cache][SRToolkit.dataset.data_cache]: this call
    writes every split without a ``data_source`` there, so the result reloads with
    [from_dict][SRToolkit.dataset.sr_dataset.SR_dataset.from_dict].

    Returns:
        A dict with ``format_version`` (``4``), ``dataset_name``, ``benchmark``, ``version``,
        ``ranking_function``, ``max_evaluations``, ``success_threshold``, ``original_equation``
        (the given string, or ``None`` when derived), ``seed``, ``dataset_metadata``, ``kwargs``,
        ``ground_truth`` (token list or ``None``),
        ``data_source``, ``test``, ``aux``, ``background_knowledge``
        ([BackgroundKnowledge.to_dict][SRToolkit.dataset.background_knowledge.BackgroundKnowledge.to_dict])
        and ``required_constraints`` (each constraint's ``to_dict``, the limit ones included).

    Raises:
        ValueError: If ``benchmark`` or ``version`` is ``None``.

    Examples:
        >>> X = np.array([[1, 2], [3, 4], [5, 6]])
        >>> dataset = SR_dataset(X, SymbolLibrary.default_symbols(2), y=np.array([3, 7, 11]),
        ...     benchmark="test", version="1.0.0")
        >>> dataset.to_dict()["format_version"]
        4
    """
    if self.benchmark is None:
        raise ValueError("[SR_dataset.to_dict] 'benchmark' is None. Set self.benchmark before serialising.")
    if self.version is None:
        raise ValueError("[SR_dataset.to_dict] 'version' is None. Set self.version before serialising.")

    # Persist any data split whose arrays are the only copy (no data_source) into the
    # cache so the returned config is reloadable by from_dict. Source-backed splits are
    # regenerated on load, so _persist_to_cache skips them and this stays side-effect-free.
    self._persist_to_cache()

    # Serialise kwargs, converting ndarray values
    kwargs_out = {}
    for k, v in self.kwargs.items():
        if isinstance(v, np.ndarray):
            kwargs_out[k] = v.tolist()
        else:
            kwargs_out[k] = v

    # Serialise ground truth (symbolic only — ndarray behaviour matrices are rejected at
    # construction and belong to the ranking function instead).
    if self.ground_truth is None:
        ground_truth_out = None
    elif isinstance(self.ground_truth, list):
        ground_truth_out = self.ground_truth
    elif isinstance(self.ground_truth, Node):
        ground_truth_out = self.ground_truth.to_list(symbol_library=self.symbol_library)
    else:
        raise ValueError("[SR_dataset.to_dict] Ground truth must be either a list or a Node")

    # The test and aux splits: which arrays each holds and where it comes from (the train
    # split's source is carried top-level as `data_source`).
    def split_entry(split: DataSplit) -> dict:
        return {
            "arrays": list(split.arrays.keys()),
            "data_source": split.data_source.to_dict() if split.data_source is not None else None,
        }

    return {
        "format_version": 4,
        "dataset_name": self.dataset_name,
        "benchmark": self.benchmark,
        "version": self.version,
        "ranking_function": self.ranking_function,
        "max_evaluations": self.max_evaluations,
        "success_threshold": self.success_threshold,
        "original_equation": self._original_equation,
        "seed": self.seed,
        "dataset_metadata": self.dataset_metadata,
        "kwargs": kwargs_out,
        "ground_truth": ground_truth_out,
        "data_source": self.data_source.to_dict() if self.data_source is not None else None,
        "test": split_entry(self.test) if self.test is not None else None,
        "aux": {key: split_entry(split) for key, split in self.aux_data.items()},
        "background_knowledge": self.background_knowledge.to_dict(),
        "required_constraints": [c.to_dict() for c in self.required_constraints],
    }

@classmethod
def from_dict(cls, d: Union[dict, str, Path]) -> "SR_dataset":
    """Load a dataset from its dictionary representation or a JSON file.

    Arrays come from the data cache, or are generated from their ``data_source``. Formats 2 and 3
    are migrated (see the [module docstring][SRToolkit.dataset.sr_dataset]). For
    ``d = ds.to_dict()``, ``from_dict(d).to_dict() == d``. Load ``.zip`` archives with
    [from_archive][SRToolkit.dataset.sr_dataset.SR_dataset.from_archive].

    Args:
        d: Output of [to_dict][SRToolkit.dataset.sr_dataset.SR_dataset.to_dict], or the path of a
            JSON file holding it.

    Returns:
        The dataset.

    Raises:
        ValueError: If ``d`` is a ``.zip`` path, ``format_version`` is not 2, 3 or 4, or the
            constructor rejects the configuration.
        TypeError: As for the constructor.
        ImportError: If a saved sampler, constraint or ranking class cannot be imported.
        FileNotFoundError: If a split's data is not in the cache and it has no ``data_source``.

    Examples:
        >>> from SRToolkit.dataset.sampling import UniformSampling
        >>> ds = SR_dataset.from_samplers(["X_0", "+", "X_1"], [UniformSampling(0, 5), UniformSampling(0, 5)],
        ...     n_samples=3, seed=0, benchmark="test_bench", version="1.0.0")
        >>> SR_dataset.from_dict(ds.to_dict()).X.shape
        (3, 2)
    """
    if isinstance(d, (str, Path)):
        if str(d).endswith(".zip"):
            raise ValueError(
                "[SR_dataset.from_dict] Received a '.zip' path. Load self-contained "
                "archives with SR_dataset.from_archive(path) instead."
            )
        with open(d) as f:
            dd = json.load(f)
    else:
        dd = dict(d)

    # Apply bundle relocation if needed
    dd = _auto_bind(dd)

    # Accept the current v4 layout and the v2 / v3 configs of earlier releases. A v2 dict has no
    # "test" / "aux" entries, so only the train split loads; its cache key is the dataset name in
    # every version, and symbolic ground truth still loads from dd["ground_truth"]. (v2 datasets
    # that stored an ndarray ground truth in a separate _gt.npy are not migrated — ndarray ground
    # truth is no longer supported; provide a symbolic ground truth or rebuild such datasets.)
    fmt = dd.get("format_version")
    if fmt not in (2, 3, 4):
        raise ValueError(f"[SR_dataset.from_dict] Unsupported format_version: {fmt!r}. Expected 2, 3 or 4.")
    # Read the task part in either layout, validating it before any data is loaded or generated.
    task_args: Dict[str, Any] = dict(dd.get("kwargs") or {})
    if "background_knowledge" in dd:  # format 4
        required = tuple(ExpressionConstraint.from_dict(c) for c in dd.get("required_constraints") or ())
        bk = BackgroundKnowledge.from_dict(dd["background_knowledge"])
        task_args.update(
            symbol_library=bk.symbol_library,
            samplers=bk.samplers,
            constant_bounds=bk.constant_bounds,
            advisory_constraints=bk.constraints,
            reference_grammar=bk.reference_grammar,
            description=bk.description,
            variables=bk.variables,
            target=bk.target,
            required_constraints=required,
            # The saved list holds the effective limits; -1 adds no default to it.
            max_constants=-1,
            max_expr_length=-1,
        )
    else:  # formats 2 and 3: symbol library and samplers at the top level, the rest in kwargs
        samplers = dd.get("samplers")
        task_args.update(
            symbol_library=SymbolLibrary.from_dict(dd["symbol_library"]),
            samplers=[Sampler.from_dict(s) for s in samplers] if samplers is not None else None,
        )

    benchmark = dd["benchmark"]
    version = dd["version"]
    dataset_name = dd["dataset_name"]

    def load_split(key: str, source_dict: Optional[dict]) -> DataSplit:
        # Resolve from the cache, materialising from the split's own source if needed. The
        # config slice keeps the dataset's samplers / ground truth, which a SampleSource needs.
        path = data_cache.resolve(benchmark, version, key, {**dd, "data_source": source_dict})
        data = np.load(str(path))
        return DataSplit({k: data[k] for k in data.files}, data_source=DataSource.from_dict(source_dict))

    train = load_split(dataset_name, dd.get("data_source"))
    test_entry = dd.get("test")
    test = load_split(f"{dataset_name}/test", test_entry.get("data_source")) if test_entry else None
    aux = {}
    for key, entry in (dd.get("aux") or {}).items():
        cls._validate_aux_key(key)
        aux[key] = load_split(f"{dataset_name}/aux/{key}", entry.get("data_source"))

    dataset = cls(
        train.X,
        ranking_function=dd["ranking_function"],
        y=train.y,
        max_evaluations=dd["max_evaluations"],
        ground_truth=dd.get("ground_truth"),
        original_equation=dd["original_equation"],
        success_threshold=dd["success_threshold"],
        seed=dd["seed"],
        dataset_metadata=dd.get("dataset_metadata"),
        dataset_name=dataset_name,
        benchmark=benchmark,
        version=version,
        **task_args,
    )
    # Attach the loaded splits whole, so every array and each split's source is kept.
    dataset._train = train
    dataset.test = test
    dataset.aux_data = aux
    return dataset

def to_archive(self, path: "Union[str, Path]") -> None:
    """Write the dataset, configuration and all data, to a self-contained ``.zip`` archive.

    The archive holds ``dataset.json`` and one ``data/<cache key>.npz`` per split, source-backed
    ones included, so loading it never regenerates or downloads anything. Like ``to_dict``, it
    writes splits without a ``data_source`` to the data cache. Load it with
    [from_archive][SRToolkit.dataset.sr_dataset.SR_dataset.from_archive] or
    [from_url][SRToolkit.dataset.sr_dataset.SR_dataset.from_url].

    Args:
        path: Destination file. A suffix other than ``.zip`` gives a warning.

    Raises:
        ValueError: If ``benchmark`` or ``version`` is ``None``.
    """
    path = Path(path)
    if path.suffix.lower() != ".zip":
        warnings.warn(
            f"[SR_dataset.to_archive] path '{path}' does not end in '.zip'. "
            "The file will be a ZIP archive regardless of the extension.",
            stacklevel=2,
        )

    # to_dict validates that benchmark/version are set.
    dataset_json = json.dumps(self.to_dict(), indent=2)

    with zipfile.ZipFile(str(path), "w", compression=zipfile.ZIP_DEFLATED) as zf:
        zf.writestr("dataset.json", dataset_json)

        for key, split in self._splits():
            buf = io.BytesIO()
            np.savez(buf, **split.arrays)  # type: ignore[arg-type]
            zf.writestr(f"data/{key}.npz", buf.getvalue())

@classmethod
def from_archive(cls, path: "Union[str, Path]") -> "SR_dataset":
    """Load a dataset from a ``.zip`` archive written by [to_archive][SRToolkit.dataset.sr_dataset.SR_dataset.to_archive].

    The archive's data is extracted into the data cache, so nothing is regenerated.

    Args:
        path: Path of the archive.

    Returns:
        The dataset.
    """
    with zipfile.ZipFile(str(path), "r") as zf:
        d = json.loads(zf.read("dataset.json"))

    benchmark = d["benchmark"]
    version = d["version"]

    # Extract every data file into the cache version directory.
    data_cache.import_archive(Path(path), benchmark, version)

    # The cache is now fully populated, so no split needs to materialise from a source.
    d["data_source"] = None
    if d.get("test"):
        d["test"]["data_source"] = None
    for entry in (d.get("aux") or {}).values():
        entry["data_source"] = None
    return cls.from_dict(d)

@classmethod
def from_url(cls, url: str) -> "SR_dataset":
    """Download an archive written by [to_archive][SRToolkit.dataset.sr_dataset.SR_dataset.to_archive] and load it.

    Loads as [from_archive][SRToolkit.dataset.sr_dataset.SR_dataset.from_archive]. For a bare data
    file, use [UrlSource][SRToolkit.dataset.data_source.UrlSource] instead.

    Args:
        url: URL of the archive.

    Returns:
        The dataset.
    """
    with urlopen(url) as response:
        data = response.read()

    tmp = tempfile.NamedTemporaryFile(suffix=".zip", delete=False)
    try:
        tmp.write(data)
        tmp.close()
        return cls.from_archive(tmp.name)
    finally:
        os.unlink(tmp.name)

@classmethod
def from_samplers(  # type: ignore[misc]
    cls,
    ground_truth: Union[List[str], Node],
    samplers: Optional[Union[List[Sampler], Mapping[str, Sampler]]] = None,
    symbol_library: Optional[SymbolLibrary] = None,
    n_samples: int = 10000,
    seed: Optional[int] = None,
    n_test: Optional[int] = None,
    ranking_function: str = "rmse",
    original_equation: Optional[str] = None,
    success_threshold: Optional[float] = None,
    max_evaluations: int = -1,
    dataset_name: str = "unnamed",
    dataset_metadata: Optional[dict] = None,
    benchmark: Optional[str] = None,
    version: Optional[str] = None,
    variables: Optional[Mapping[str, VariableInfo]] = None,
    target: Optional[VariableInfo] = None,
    description: Optional[str] = None,
    constant_bounds: Optional[Tuple[float, float]] = None,
    reference_grammar: Optional[Grammar] = None,
    max_constants: Optional[int] = None,
    max_expr_length: Optional[int] = None,
    required_constraints: Optional[Iterable[ExpressionConstraint]] = None,
    advisory_constraints: Optional[Iterable[ExpressionConstraint]] = None,
    **kwargs: Unpack[RankingSettings],
) -> "SR_dataset":
    """Build a dataset by sampling inputs and evaluating a ground truth on them.

    ``X`` is drawn from the samplers and ``y`` is computed as in
    [resample][SRToolkit.dataset.sr_dataset.SR_dataset.resample]. The data gets a
    [SampleSource][SRToolkit.dataset.data_source.SampleSource] as ``data_source``, so ``to_dict``
    stores no arrays and [refresh][SRToolkit.dataset.sr_dataset.SR_dataset.refresh] regenerates it.

    Args:
        ground_truth: The answer as infix tokens or a [Node][SRToolkit.utils.expression_tree.Node];
            it must have no free constants unless ``ranking_function`` is ``"bed"``.
        samplers: One [Sampler][SRToolkit.dataset.sampling.Sampler] per variable, as a list in
            variable order or ``{token: sampler}``.
        symbol_library: ``None`` uses
            [default_symbols][SRToolkit.utils.symbol_library.SymbolLibrary.default_symbols] with one
            variable per sampler.
        n_samples: Number of rows of ``X``.
        seed: Seed of the draw, stored on the ``SampleSource``; ``None`` for none.
        n_test: Rows of a held-out test split drawn the same way with seed ``seed + 1``, with its own
            ``SampleSource``; ``None`` for no test split.
        ranking_function: As for ``SR_dataset``; with ``"bed"`` no ``y`` is generated.
        original_equation: As for ``SR_dataset``.
        success_threshold: As for ``SR_dataset``.
        max_evaluations: As for ``SR_dataset``.
        dataset_name: As for ``SR_dataset``.
        dataset_metadata: As for ``SR_dataset``.
        benchmark: As for ``SR_dataset``.
        version: As for ``SR_dataset``.
        variables: As for ``SR_dataset``.
        target: As for ``SR_dataset``.
        description: As for ``SR_dataset``.
        constant_bounds: As for ``SR_dataset``.
        reference_grammar: As for ``SR_dataset``.
        max_constants: As for ``SR_dataset``.
        max_expr_length: As for ``SR_dataset``.
        required_constraints: As for ``SR_dataset``.
        advisory_constraints: As for ``SR_dataset``.
        **kwargs: As for ``SR_dataset``.

    Returns:
        The dataset with freshly generated data.

    Raises:
        ValueError: If ``samplers`` is ``None`` or empty, ``y`` cannot be computed (see ``resample``),
            or the constructor rejects the arguments.
        TypeError: As for the constructor.

    Examples:
        >>> from SRToolkit.dataset.sampling import UniformSampling
        >>> ds = SR_dataset.from_samplers(["X_0", "+", "X_1"],
        ...     [UniformSampling(0, 5), UniformSampling(0, 5)], n_samples=100, seed=0)
        >>> ds.X.shape
        (100, 2)
        >>> ds.original_equation
        'y = X_0+X_1'
    """
    if not samplers:
        raise ValueError(
            "[SR_dataset.from_samplers] 'samplers' must be non-empty (one sampler per input variable)."
        )
    n_vars = len(samplers)
    if symbol_library is None:
        symbol_library = SymbolLibrary.default_symbols(n_vars)

    dataset = cls(
        np.empty((0, n_vars)),
        symbol_library,
        ranking_function=ranking_function,
        ground_truth=ground_truth,
        original_equation=original_equation,
        success_threshold=success_threshold,
        max_evaluations=max_evaluations,
        dataset_name=dataset_name,
        dataset_metadata=dataset_metadata,
        samplers=samplers,
        benchmark=benchmark,
        version=version,
        variables=variables,
        target=target,
        description=description,
        constant_bounds=constant_bounds,
        reference_grammar=reference_grammar,
        max_constants=max_constants,
        max_expr_length=max_expr_length,
        required_constraints=required_constraints,
        advisory_constraints=advisory_constraints,
        **kwargs,
    )
    dataset.data_source = SampleSource(n_samples=n_samples, seed=seed)

    # Reuse the canonical generation path (handles rmse/bed and its validation).
    dataset.resample_inplace(n_samples, seed=seed)

    # Optional held-out test split: same samplers + ground truth, its own source/seed.
    if n_test is not None:
        test_seed = None if seed is None else seed + 1
        test_result = dataset.resample(n_test, seed=test_seed)
        if isinstance(test_result, tuple):
            test_arrays: Dict[str, np.ndarray] = {"X": test_result[0], "y": test_result[1]}
        else:
            test_arrays = {"X": test_result}
        dataset.test = DataSplit(test_arrays, data_source=SampleSource(n_samples=n_test, seed=test_seed))

    return dataset

def refresh(self) -> None:
    """Regenerate every split that has a ``data_source`` and reload it.

    The new arrays overwrite the split's files in the data cache.

    Raises:
        ValueError: If ``data_source``, ``benchmark`` or ``version`` is ``None``.
    """
    if self.data_source is None:
        raise ValueError(
            "[SR_dataset.refresh] Cannot refresh: data_source is null. "
            "Set self.data_source to a valid source config before calling refresh()."
        )
    if self.benchmark is None or self.version is None:
        raise ValueError("[SR_dataset.refresh] Cannot refresh: 'benchmark' or 'version' is None.")

    config = self.to_dict()
    for key, split in self._splits():
        if split.data_source is None:
            continue
        cache_path = data_cache.resolve(
            self.benchmark,
            self.version,
            key,
            {**config, "data_source": split.data_source.to_dict()},
            force=True,
        )
        data = np.load(str(cache_path))
        split.arrays = {k: data[k] for k in data.files}

SRSD_Feynman(n_samples: int = 10000, seed: Optional[int] = 42, force_generate: bool = False)

Bases: SR_benchmark

The SRSD Feynman symbolic regression benchmark.

Contains 120 physics equations from the Feynman Symbolic Regression Dataset with per-variable sampling strategies (log-uniform, linear, or integer with sign constraints). Data is generated on first instantiation and cached as .npz files for subsequent use.

Warning

Seven datasets currently have a known data problem, both in the downloaded data and with force_generate=True:

  • SRSD II.24.17, SRSD Bonus 4 and SRSD Bonus 7: for part of the sampled points (about 25–85%) the ground truth takes the square root of a negative number, so y contains NaN. The ground truth itself then scores NaN, so no approach can be counted as solving these datasets.
  • SRSD II.6.15a, SRSD II.6.15b, SRSD III.19.51 and SRSD Bonus 12: y reaches 1e16 to 1e24, so rounding alone gives the ground truth an RMSE between about 1e-3 and 3e6. Whether it counts as a success depends on success_threshold.

Leave these datasets out, or read their results with care, until this is fixed.

References

Matsubara et al. (2024)

Examples:

>>> benchmark = SRSD_Feynman()
>>> len(benchmark.list_datasets(verbose=False))
120

docs.title: SRToolkit.dataset.background_knowledge
docs.text:
What a symbolic regression task tells the approach besides the data.

BackgroundKnowledge collects what a dataset deliberately gives the approach that solves it:

  • the symbols expressions may use (the symbol library),
  • the input distribution (one Sampler per variable),
  • the range free constants are fitted in (constant_bounds),
  • advisory ExpressionConstraints: hints about the search space that an approach may use or ignore,
  • an optional reference Grammar (rule weights a grammar-based approach can start from),
  • a description of the task, of each variable and of the target (VariableInfo: name and description).

Priors about the answer's form are advisory constraints: each has a text form (describe) and a record form (summary), and priors lists the records. A prior that cannot be checked is a constraint that implements neither check: the evaluator skips it, and it is still described. Anything else goes into description.

SR_dataset builds one from its arguments (symbol_library=, samplers=, advisory_constraints=, ...). Physical units of variables are not part of it yet.

docs.title: What it does not hold
docs.text:
The answer stays out: the ground truth, the human-readable equation, the success threshold and anything derived from them live on SR_dataset, not here. describe renders only background knowledge, so its text can go into a prompt without leaking the answer (unlike str(dataset), which starts with the equation).

Required constraints are not background knowledge either: they are part of the objective and live on the dataset (SR_dataset.required_constraints). Advisory and required constraints are the same classes; the list a constraint is in decides its role (see expression_constraints).

def describe(self) -> str:
    """Return a one-line description: ``"<name>: <description>"``.

docs.text:
describe(required_constraints: Iterable[ExpressionConstraint] = ()) -> str

Return a plain-text description of the task for people and LLM prompts.

Contains nothing about the answer. Lines, in this order, each left out when its field is empty or None:

  • Task: <description>
  • Target: <target.describe()> (also left out if that is "")
  • Variables: then one line <token>: <VariableInfo.describe()> per entry of variables, in the library's variable order (just <token> if it describes to "")
  • Symbols: <str(symbol_library)> (always present)
  • Free constants are fitted in [<lower>, <upper>]., bounds written with str of a float (only if the library has a "const" symbol)
  • Input distribution: then <token>: <sampler> per variable (only with samplers)
  • Enforced constraints (expressions that break them are rejected): then - <constraint> per required constraint
  • Hints (advisory, may be ignored): then - <constraint> per advisory constraint
  • Reference grammar: given

A constraint is written as its describe, e.g. expression tree at most 4 levels deep. A sampler is written as its describe, e.g. uniform on [1, 5].

      ``variables``, in the library's variable order (just ``  <token>`` if it describes to
      ``""``)
    - ``Symbols: <str(symbol_library)>`` (always present)
    - ``Free constants are fitted in [<lower>, <upper>].``, bounds written with ``str`` of a
      ``float`` (only if the library has a ``"const"`` symbol)
    - ``Input distribution:`` then ``  <token>: <sampler>`` per variable (only with samplers)
    - ``Enforced constraints (expressions that break them are rejected):`` then
      ``  - <constraint>`` per required constraint
    - ``Hints (advisory, may be ignored):`` then ``  - <constraint>`` per advisory constraint
    - ``Reference grammar: given``

    A constraint is written as its
    [describe][SRToolkit.utils.expression_constraints.ExpressionConstraint.describe], e.g.
    ``expression tree at most 4 levels deep``. A sampler is written as its
    [describe][SRToolkit.dataset.sampling.Sampler.describe], e.g. ``uniform on [1, 5]``.

    Args:
        required_constraints: The dataset's required constraints, listed apart from the
            advisory ones. Empty when called on its own;
            [SR_dataset.describe][SRToolkit.dataset.sr_dataset.SR_dataset.describe] passes the
            dataset's.

    Returns:
        The description, lines separated by ``"\n"``, without a trailing newline.

    Examples:
        >>> from SRToolkit.utils import SymbolLibrary
        >>> bk = BackgroundKnowledge(SymbolLibrary.from_symbol_list(["+", "*"], num_variables=1),
        ...     description="Toy task", variables={"X_0": VariableInfo("x", "position")})
        >>> print(bk.describe())
        Task: Toy task
        Variables:
          X_0: x: position
        Symbols: +, *, X_0
    """
    lines: List[str] = []
    if self.description:
        lines.append(f"Task: {self.description}")
    if self.target is not None and self.target.describe():
        lines.append(f"Target: {self.target.describe()}")
    if self.variables:
        lines.append("Variables:")
        for token, info in self.variables.items():
            text = info.describe()
            lines.append(f"  {token}: {text}" if text else f"  {token}")
    lines.append(f"Symbols: {self.symbol_library}")
    if self.symbol_library.get_symbols_of_type("const"):
        lower, upper = self.constant_bounds
        lines.append(f"Free constants are fitted in [{lower}, {upper}].")
    if self.samplers is not None and len(self.samplers) > 0:
        lines.append("Input distribution:")
        samplers = cast(Tuple[Sampler, ...], self.samplers)  # normalised to a tuple in __post_init__
        for token, sampler in zip(self.symbol_library.get_symbols_of_type("var"), samplers):
            lines.append(f"  {token}: {sampler.describe()}")
    required = tuple(required_constraints)
    if required:
        lines.append("Enforced constraints (expressions that break them are rejected):")
        lines.extend(f"  - {c.describe()}" for c in required)
    if self.constraints:
        lines.append("Hints (advisory, may be ignored):")
        lines.extend(f"  - {c.describe()}" for c in self.constraints)
    if self.reference_grammar is not None:
        lines.append("Reference grammar: given")
    return "\n".join(lines)

def to_dict(self) -> dict:
    """Return a JSON-safe dictionary of this background knowledge.

    Returns:
        A dictionary with ``"format_version": 1`` and one key per field, named as the field:
        ``symbol_library``, ``reference_grammar`` (or ``None``) and each sampler and constraint
        as their own ``to_dict``; ``samplers`` as a list in the library's variable order (or
        ``None``); ``constant_bounds`` as ``[lower, upper]``; ``variables`` as
        ``{token: VariableInfo.to_dict()}`` in the library's variable order; ``target`` as its
        ``to_dict`` (or ``None``); ``description`` as given.
    """
    return {
        "format_version": 1,
        "symbol_library": self.symbol_library.to_dict(),
        "samplers": (
            [s.to_dict() for s in cast(Tuple[Sampler, ...], self.samplers)] if self.samplers is not None else None
        ),
        "constant_bounds": list(self.constant_bounds),
        "constraints": [c.to_dict() for c in self.constraints],
        "reference_grammar": self.reference_grammar.to_dict() if self.reference_grammar is not None else None,
        "description": self.description,
        "variables": {token: info.to_dict() for token, info in self.variables.items()},
        "target": self.target.to_dict() if self.target is not None else None,
    }

@classmethod
def from_dict(cls, d: dict) -> "BackgroundKnowledge":
    """Rebuild background knowledge from the output of ``to_dict``.

    Missing keys other than ``symbol_library`` take their defaults (a missing
    ``format_version`` is read as ``1``); unknown keys are ignored.

    Args:
        d: A dictionary produced by
            [to_dict][SRToolkit.dataset.background_knowledge.BackgroundKnowledge.to_dict].

    Returns:
        Background knowledge whose ``to_dict`` equals ``d`` with missing keys filled in.

    Raises:
        KeyError: If ``symbol_library`` is missing.
        ValueError: If ``format_version`` is not ``1``, or as for the constructor.
        TypeError: As for the constructor.
        ImportError: If a saved sampler or constraint class cannot be imported.
    """
    fmt = d.get("format_version", 1)
    if fmt != 1:
        raise ValueError(f"[BackgroundKnowledge.from_dict] Unsupported format_version: {fmt!r}. Expected 1.")
    library = SymbolLibrary.from_dict(d["symbol_library"])
    samplers = d.get("samplers")
    grammar = d.get("reference_grammar")
    target = d.get("target")
    return cls(
        symbol_library=library,
        samplers=[Sampler.from_dict(s) for s in samplers] if samplers is not None else None,
        constant_bounds=tuple(d.get("constant_bounds", (-5.0, 5.0))),  # type: ignore[arg-type]
        constraints=[ExpressionConstraint.from_dict(c) for c in d.get("constraints") or ()],
        reference_grammar=Grammar.from_dict(grammar) if grammar is not None else None,
        description=d.get("description", ""),
        variables={k: VariableInfo.from_dict(v) for k, v in (d.get("variables") or {}).items()},
        target=VariableInfo.from_dict(target) if target is not None else None,
    )

def resolve(
    benchmark: str,
    version: str,
    key: str,
    config: Optional[dict] = None,
    *,
    force: bool = False,
) -> Path:
    """Return the cache path for ``<benchmark>/<version>/<key>.npz``, materialising it if needed.

    The data source is reconstructed from ``config["data_source"]`` via
    [DataSource.from_dict][SRToolkit.dataset.data_source.DataSource.from_dict]. Passing
    ``config=None`` (or a config whose ``"data_source"`` is ``None``) is valid only when
    the cache entry already exists — it asserts presence without triggering
    materialisation.

    On a cache hit (file exists and ``force`` is ``False``): if the source is *volatile*
    (e.g. [SampleSource][SRToolkit.dataset.data_source.SampleSource]), the stored sidecar
    ``.meta.json`` hash is compared against the current ``data_source`` + ``samplers``
    config. A mismatch emits a warning telling the user to call ``refresh()``. The samplers are
    read from either config layout (see ``config``), and the hash does not depend on the layout,
    so a format 2/3 config and its format 4 migration hash the same.

    On a cache miss (or ``force=True``): the data is materialised by calling the source's
    [materialize][SRToolkit.dataset.data_source.DataSource.materialize].

    Args:
        benchmark: Benchmark name (e.g. ``"feynman"``).
        version: Version string (e.g. ``"1.0.0"``).
        key: Dataset key / name (e.g. ``"I.16.6"``).
        config: Full dataset config dict containing a ``"data_source"`` key, in format 4
            (symbol library and samplers inside ``"background_knowledge"``, as written by
            [SR_dataset.to_dict][SRToolkit.dataset.sr_dataset.SR_dataset.to_dict]) or in the
            format 2/3 layout (``"symbol_library"`` and ``"samplers"`` at the top level).
            ``None`` (or a config with ``data_source=None``) is valid only when
            the cache entry already exists.
        force: If ``True``, re-materialise even when the cache entry exists.

    Returns:
        Path to the ``.npz`` file in the cache.

    Raises:
        FileNotFoundError: If the cache entry is absent and no source is available.
    """
    from SRToolkit.dataset.data_source import DataSource

    source_dict = config.get("data_source") if config is not None else None
    source = DataSource.from_dict(source_dict)
    cache_path = dataset_path(benchmark, version, key)

    if cache_path.exists() and not force:
        # Drift detection: if the data_source / samplers config no longer matches what
        # the cache was built from, the cached bytes may be stale. This applies to any
        # source — a SampleSource whose n_samples/seed changed, a UrlSource whose url
        # changed, or a switch between source kinds (e.g. UrlSource ↔ SampleSource).
        if source is not None and config is not None:
            meta = _read_meta(cache_path)
            if meta is not None and meta.get("source_hash") != _drift_hash(config):
                warnings.warn(
                    f"[dataset.data_cache.resolve] The data_source config for '{benchmark}/{key}' has changed "
                    f"since the cache was built. Call refresh() to regenerate the data.",
                    stacklevel=3,
                )
        return cache_path

    # Need to materialise
    if source is None or config is None:  # Second condition is just for the type checker
        raise FileNotFoundError(
            f"[dataset.data_cache.resolve] No cached data found for '{benchmark}/{version}/{key}' "
            f"and data_source is None. Provide a data_source or import the data manually."
        )

    source.materialize(cache_path, config)
    _write_meta(cache_path, config)

    return cache_path

extract_zip_into_version_dir(zf: ZipFile, version_dir: Path, *, flat_fallback: bool = True) -> None

Extract an open ZipFile into version_dir, accepting both archive layouts.

  • to_archive layout: data files live under a data/ prefix (alongside a benchmark.json / dataset.json that is not a data file). The data/ prefix is stripped so the .npz files land in the version directory (a dataset's test and aux data in its own subfolder); non-data/ members are ignored.
  • flat layout: the .npz files sit at the archive root (as served by the built-in benchmarks). When flat_fallback is True (the default) and no data/-prefixed member is present, the whole archive is extracted as-is.

The layout is detected automatically by the presence of any data/-prefixed member, so a single hosted to_archive archive can be consumed both by SR_benchmark.from_url and by a config carrying a UrlSource.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default zf ZipFile

An open ZipFile to extract.

required version_dir Path

Destination cache version directory.

required flat_fallback bool

If True, an archive with no data/ prefix is extracted in full (flat layout). If False, such an archive yields nothing — only data/-prefixed members are ever extracted. import_archive uses False so stray metadata files never land in the cache version directory.

True Source code in SRToolkit/dataset/data_cache.py 
def extract_zip_into_version_dir(zf: zipfile.ZipFile, version_dir: Path, *, flat_fallback: bool = True) -> None:
    """Extract an open ``ZipFile`` into ``version_dir``, accepting both archive layouts.

    - **``to_archive`` layout**: data files live under a ``data/`` prefix (alongside a
      ``benchmark.json`` / ``dataset.json`` that is *not* a data file). The ``data/``
      prefix is stripped so the ``.npz`` files land in the version directory (a dataset's test
      and aux data in its own subfolder); non-``data/`` members are ignored.
    - **flat layout**: the ``.npz`` files sit at the archive root (as served by the
      built-in benchmarks). When ``flat_fallback`` is ``True`` (the default) and no
      ``data/``-prefixed member is present, the whole archive is extracted as-is.

    The layout is detected automatically by the presence of any ``data/``-prefixed
    member, so a single hosted ``to_archive`` archive can be consumed both by
    [SR_benchmark.from_url][SRToolkit.dataset.sr_benchmark.SR_benchmark.from_url] and by a
    config carrying a [UrlSource][SRToolkit.dataset.data_source.UrlSource].

    Args:
        zf: An open ``ZipFile`` to extract.
        version_dir: Destination cache version directory.
        flat_fallback: If ``True``, an archive with no ``data/`` prefix is extracted in
            full (flat layout). If ``False``, such an archive yields nothing — only
            ``data/``-prefixed members are ever extracted. [import_archive][SRToolkit.dataset.data_cache.import_archive]
            uses ``False`` so stray metadata files never land in the cache version directory.
    """
    members = zf.infolist()
    has_data_prefix = any(m.filename.startswith("data/") for m in members)

    if not has_data_prefix:
        if flat_fallback:
            zf.extractall(path=str(version_dir))
        return

    for member in members:
        name = member.filename
        if not name.startswith("data/"):
            continue
        # Strip the "data/" prefix
        relative = name[len("data/") :]
        if not relative:
            continue  # Skip the directory entry itself
        target = version_dir / relative
        # Guard against zip-slip: the archive may be downloaded from an untrusted URL,
        # so refuse members that resolve outside the destination version directory.
        resolved_dir = version_dir.resolve()
        resolved_target = target.resolve()
        if resolved_dir != resolved_target and resolved_dir not in resolved_target.parents:
            raise ValueError(
                f"[extract_zip_into_version_dir] Refusing to extract '{name}': resolves outside the "
                f"destination directory (possible zip-slip)."
            )
        target.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        target.write_bytes(zf.read(member.filename))

def import_archive(archive_path: Path, benchmark: str, version: str) -> None:
    """Extract a ``.zip`` archive into the cache version directory
    ``<data_root>/<benchmark>/<version_slug>/``.

    Both the ``to_archive`` layout (data under a ``data/`` prefix) and a flat layout
    (``.npz`` files at the archive root) are handled — see
    [extract_zip_into_version_dir][SRToolkit.dataset.data_cache.extract_zip_into_version_dir].

    Args:
        archive_path: Path to a ``.zip`` file (e.g. a benchmark ``.zip``).
        benchmark: Benchmark name used to determine the cache directory.
        version: Version string used to determine the cache directory.
    """
    slug = _version_slug(version)
    version_dir = data_root() / benchmark / slug
    version_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)

    with zipfile.ZipFile(str(archive_path), "r") as zf:
        extract_zip_into_version_dir(zf, version_dir, flat_fallback=False)

def list() -> List[Dict[str, Any]]:
    """List all datasets currently stored in the cache.

    Walks ``data_root()`` and returns one dict per cached dataset (its main ``.npz``; a
    dataset's test and aux data in its subfolder are not listed separately).

    Returns:
        A list of dicts, each with keys ``benchmark``, ``version``, ``key``,
        ``path``, and ``size_bytes``.
    """
    root = data_root()
    entries: List[Dict[str, Any]] = []
    if not root.exists():
        return entries

    for benchmark_dir in sorted(root.iterdir()):
        if not benchmark_dir.is_dir():
            continue
        benchmark = benchmark_dir.name
        for version_dir in sorted(benchmark_dir.iterdir()):
            if not version_dir.is_dir():
                continue
            version_slug = version_dir.name
            # Convert slug back to version string (underscores → dots)
            version = version_slug.replace("_", ".")
            for npz_file in sorted(version_dir.glob("*.npz")):
                entries.append(
                    {
                        "benchmark": benchmark,
                        "version": version,
                        "key": npz_file.stem,
                        "path": str(npz_file),
                        "size_bytes": npz_file.stat().st_size,
                    }
                )
    return entries

def gc(keep_latest: bool = True) -> List[Path]:
    """Garbage-collect the data cache.

    Args:
        keep_latest: If ``True`` (default), retain only the latest version
            (by semantic version ordering) per benchmark and delete all older
            versions. If ``False``, wipes the entire cache.

    Returns:
        A list of ``Path`` objects that were removed.
    """
    root = data_root()
    removed: List[Path] = []
    if not root.exists():
        return removed

    for benchmark_dir in sorted(root.iterdir()):
        if not benchmark_dir.is_dir():
            continue

        version_dirs = [d for d in benchmark_dir.iterdir() if d.is_dir()]
        if not version_dirs:
            continue

        if not keep_latest:
            for vdir in version_dirs:
                shutil.rmtree(vdir)
                removed.append(vdir)
            continue

        # Determine latest version
        def _slug_to_version(slug: str) -> Any:
            ver_str = slug.replace("_", ".")
            if PkgVersion is not None:
                try:
                    return PkgVersion(ver_str)
                except Exception:
                    return ver_str
            return ver_str

        sorted_dirs = sorted(version_dirs, key=lambda d: _slug_to_version(d.name))
        for vdir in sorted_dirs[:-1]:
            shutil.rmtree(vdir)
            removed.append(vdir)

    return removed

def remove(benchmark: str, version: Optional[str] = None, key: Optional[str] = None) -> List[Path]:
    """Remove a specific cached benchmark, version, or dataset.

    The deletion granularity widens as fewer arguments are given:

    - ``remove("feynman")`` — delete every cached version of the benchmark.
    - ``remove("feynman", "1.0.0")`` — delete just that version directory.
    - ``remove("feynman", "1.0.0", "I.16.6")`` — delete a single dataset: its ``.npz``, its
      ``.meta.json`` sidecar, and its folder holding the test and aux data (plus a ``_gt.npy``
      left by older versions).

    Targeting something that is not in the cache is a no-op (returns an empty list);
    nothing is raised.

    Args:
        benchmark: Benchmark name (e.g. ``"feynman"``).
        version: Version string. If ``None``, the whole benchmark is removed.
        key: Dataset key / name. If ``None``, the whole version directory is removed.

    Returns:
        List of paths that were removed.
    """
    removed: List[Path] = []
    root = data_root()
    if not root.exists():
        return removed

    benchmark_dir = root / benchmark
    if not benchmark_dir.is_dir():
        return removed

    if version is None:
        shutil.rmtree(benchmark_dir)
        removed.append(benchmark_dir)
        return removed

    version_dir = benchmark_dir / _version_slug(version)
    if not version_dir.is_dir():
        return removed

    if key is None:
        shutil.rmtree(version_dir)
        removed.append(version_dir)
    else:
        npz_path = version_dir / f"{key}.npz"
        for target in (npz_path, version_dir / f"{key}_gt.npy", _meta_path(npz_path)):
            if target.exists():
                target.unlink()
                removed.append(target)
        # The dataset's test and aux data live in a folder named after it.
        splits_dir = version_dir / key
        if splits_dir.is_dir():
            shutil.rmtree(splits_dir)
            removed.append(splits_dir)

    return removed

docs.title: SRToolkit.dataset.data_source
docs.text:
Data-source descriptors for symbolic regression datasets.

A DataSource describes the origin of a dataset's data (where the X / y arrays come from). This is a separate concern from the dataset's input-distribution spec (its samplers): the samplers define what the inputs of the problem look like and power resample, and remain available no matter where the data originated.

Two concrete sources ship with the toolkit:

  • UrlSource — download a .zip from a URL and extract it into the cache.
  • SampleSource — generate the data by drawing n_samples points from the dataset's samplers.

A data_source of None means the data was supplied directly (e.g. as arrays) and already lives in the cache; nothing needs to be materialised.

Sources serialize via a "source_class" key holding the fully-qualified class path, mirroring other custom classes, e.g., Sampler. As a result DataSource.from_dict can reconstruct any subclass — including user-defined ones — via importlib without a central registry: subclass DataSource, implement to_dict / from_dict / materialize, and it round-trips. Custom sources only travel to other machines via the bundle mechanism (their code must be importable on the other end). Because reconstruction imports the class named in the config, only load configs you trust.

The dict produced by to_dict must include a "source_class" key holding the fully-qualified class path (e.g. "SRToolkit.dataset.data_source.UrlSource") so that DataSource.from_dict can reconstruct it via importlib without a central registry.

The cache layer stores a hash of every source's data_source + samplers config and warns when it drifts from what the cache was built with — regardless of this flag — so a changed url, changed n_samples/seed, or a switch between source kinds is always surfaced.
