def evaluate_expr(
    self,
    expr: Union[List[str], Node],
    simplify_expr: bool = False,
    verbose: int = 0,
) -> float:
    """Evaluate an expression, or return its cached error.

    A new expression is parsed, checked against the constraints, scored by the ranking
    function and stored in ``models`` (statuses and the order of checks are in the
    [module docs][SRToolkit.evaluation.sr_evaluator]). An expression evaluated before is not
    scored again; its stored error is returned. Either way the call is appended to ``trace``,
    counts toward ``max_evaluations`` and is reported to the callbacks: ``on_expr_evaluated``
    for every call, plus ``on_best_expression`` when the error improves on the best so far. A
    callback returning ``False`` stops evaluation; by default this happens when an error is
    below ``success_threshold`` or ``max_evaluations`` is reached.

    Note:
        ``simplify_expr=True`` makes a call much slower: simplifying with SymPy usually takes
        longer than scoring the expression. Use it to inspect the best results after a search,
        not on every candidate during it.

    Examples:
        >>> X = np.array([[1, 2], [8, 4], [5, 4], [7, 9]])
        >>> y = np.array([3, 0, 3, 11])
        >>> se = SR_evaluator(X, y, seed=42)
        >>> print(se.evaluate_expr(["C", "*", "X_1", "-", "X_0"]) < 1e-6)
        True
        >>> # With simplify_expr, the simplified expression is scored and stored
        >>> X = np.array([[0, 1], [0, 2], [0, 3]])
        >>> se = SR_evaluator(X, np.array([2, 3, 4]), seed=42, success_threshold=-1)
        >>> _ = se.evaluate_expr(["C", "+", "C", "*", "C", "+", "X_0", "*", "X_1", "/", "X_0"], simplify_expr=True)
        >>> "".join(se.models[0].expr), bool(0.99 < se.models[0].parameters[0] < 1.01)
        ('C+X_1', True)
        >>> # A malformed expression gets the error inf and the status "invalid"
        >>> print(se.evaluate_expr(["C", "*", "X_1", "X_0"]))
        inf
        >>> se.models[-1].status
        'invalid'
        >>> # BED is stochastic and scaled by the ground truth's output, so an exact match may
        >>> # still have a small positive error
        >>> X = np.random.rand(10, 2) - 0.5
        >>> se = SR_evaluator(X, ground_truth=["X_0", "+", "C"], ranking_function="bed", seed=42)
        >>> print(se.evaluate_expr(["C", "+", "X_0"]) < 0.2)
        True

    Args:
        expr: The expression, as a token list in infix notation or a
            [Node][SRToolkit.utils.expression_tree.Node] tree.
        simplify_expr: If ``True``, simplify the expression first; the simplified
            expression is then checked, scored, cached and stored as ``ModelResult.expr``, so
            inputs that simplify alike share one cache entry. If simplification fails, a
            warning is emitted and the expression is evaluated as given. Default ``False``.
        verbose: ``0`` (default): no logging. ``1``: log at DEBUG level (logger
            ``SRToolkit.evaluation.sr_evaluator``) each new expression with its final status,
            error and ``status_detail``, and each cache hit. ``2``: also let NumPy
            floating-point warnings through while scoring.

    Returns:
        The error under the active ranking function, or ``+inf`` if the status is not
        ``"ok"``. ``nan`` if evaluation has already stopped: the call then emits a warning and
        is not counted.

    Raises:
        TypeError: If ``expr`` is neither a token list nor a ``Node``.
    """
    if self.should_stop:
        warnings.warn(
            f"Evaluation stopped because max_evaluations ({self.max_evaluations}) reached or an expression with error lower than success_threshold ({self.success_threshold}) was found. "
        )
        return np.nan
    else:
        if simplify_expr:
            try:
                expr = simplify(expr, self.symbol_library)
            except Exception as e:
                expr_list = _as_tokens(expr, self.symbol_library)
                warnings.warn(f"Unable to simplify: {''.join(expr_list)}, problems with subexpression {e}")

        expr_list = _as_tokens(expr, self.symbol_library)

        expr_str = "".join(expr_list)
        index = self._model_index.get(expr_str)
        if index is not None:
            if verbose > 0:
                logger.debug("Already evaluated %s", expr_str)
            self.trace.append(index)
            if self._callbacks is not None:
                event = ExprEvaluated(
                    expression=expr_str,
                    error=self.models[index].error,
                    evaluation_number=self.total_evaluations,
                    experiment_id=self._experiment_id,
                    is_new_best=False,
                    status=self.models[index].status,
                )
                if not self._callbacks.on_expr_evaluated(event):
                    self.should_stop = True
            return self.models[index].error

        else:
            model = self._evaluate_new(expr, expr_list, expr_str, verbose)
            if verbose > 0:
                logger.debug(
                    "Evaluated expression %s: status %s, error %s%s",
                    expr_str,
                    model.status,
                    model.error,
                    f" ({model.status_detail})" if model.status_detail else "",
                )
            error = model.error
            self._model_index[expr_str] = len(self.models)
            self.trace.append(len(self.models))
            self.models.append(model)

            if self._callbacks is not None:
                is_new_best = error < self._current_best_error
                if is_new_best:
                    self._current_best_error = error
                event = ExprEvaluated(
                    expression=expr_str,
                    error=error,
                    evaluation_number=self.total_evaluations,
                    experiment_id=self._experiment_id,
                    is_new_best=is_new_best,
                    status=model.status,
                )
                if not self._callbacks.on_expr_evaluated(event):
                    self.should_stop = True
                if is_new_best:
                    best_event = BestExpressionFound(
                        experiment_id=self._experiment_id,
                        expression=expr_str,
                        error=error,
                        evaluation_number=self.total_evaluations,
                    )
                    if not self._callbacks.on_best_expression(best_event):
                        self.should_stop = True

            return error

get_metric(expr: Union[List[str], Node], metric: Union[str, Callable[[Callable[[ndarray], ndarray], ndarray, ndarray], float]] = 'r2') -> float

Compute an alternative, read-only metric for an already-evaluated expression.

Unlike evaluate_expr, this does not count toward the evaluation budget, does not affect ranking, success, caching, or callbacks, and never changes the canonical ranking function. It exists so an approach can structure its search around a measure other than the ranking error (e.g. R² or NRMSE) without re-running the (budgeted) evaluation and without being given direct access to X/y as attributes.

The expression must already have been evaluated via evaluate_expr so its constants are fitted and cached — otherwise a ValueError is raised. This is the guard that keeps the budget meaningful: a custom metric callable cannot be used to score un-evaluated expressions for free.

The metric is computed from a constants-bound prediction function predict(X) -> y_pred built from the cached fit. Built-in string metrics and custom callables share the signature metric(predict, X, y) -> float; passing predict (rather than a precomputed y_pred) lets a metric also evaluate the model away from X (e.g. for smoothness or extrapolation measures).

Only available in ranking_function="rmse" mode. In BED mode (no y, no fitted constants), and for models that could not be scored (status other than "ok"), this returns NaN.

Examples:

>>> X = np.array([[1, 2], [8, 4], [5, 4], [7, 9]])
>>> y = np.array([3, 0, 3, 11])
>>> se = SR_evaluator(X, y, seed=42)
>>> _ = se.evaluate_expr(["C", "*", "X_1", "-", "X_0"])
>>> print(se.get_metric(["C", "*", "X_1", "-", "X_0"], "r2") > 0.999)
True
>>> # A custom measure: worst-case absolute residual.
>>> def max_abs_residual(predict, X, y):
...     return float(np.max(np.abs(predict(X) - y)))
>>> print(se.get_metric(["C", "*", "X_1", "-", "X_0"], max_abs_residual) < 1e-6)
True

def get_metric(
    self,
    expr: Union[List[str], Node],
    metric: Union[str, Callable[[Callable[[np.ndarray], np.ndarray], np.ndarray, np.ndarray], float]] = "r2",
) -> float:
    """Compute an alternative, read-only metric for an already-evaluated expression.

    Unlike [evaluate_expr][SRToolkit.evaluation.sr_evaluator.SR_evaluator.evaluate_expr],
    this does **not** count toward the evaluation budget, does not affect ranking,
    success, caching, or callbacks, and never changes the canonical ranking function.
    It exists so an approach can structure its search around a measure other than the
    ranking error (e.g. R² or NRMSE) without re-running the (budgeted) evaluation and
    without being given direct access to ``X``/``y`` as attributes.

    The expression **must already have been evaluated** via ``evaluate_expr`` so its
    constants are fitted and cached — otherwise a ``ValueError`` is raised. This is the
    guard that keeps the budget meaningful: a custom ``metric`` callable cannot be used to
    score un-evaluated expressions for free.

    The ``metric`` is computed from a constants-bound prediction function
    ``predict(X) -> y_pred`` built from the cached fit. Built-in string metrics and
    custom callables share the signature ``metric(predict, X, y) -> float``; passing
    ``predict`` (rather than a precomputed ``y_pred``) lets a metric also evaluate the
    model away from ``X`` (e.g. for smoothness or extrapolation measures).

    Only available in ``ranking_function="rmse"`` mode. In BED mode (no ``y``,
    no fitted constants), and for models that could not be scored (status other than
    ``"ok"``), this returns ``NaN``.

    Examples:
        >>> X = np.array([[1, 2], [8, 4], [5, 4], [7, 9]])
        >>> y = np.array([3, 0, 3, 11])
        >>> se = SR_evaluator(X, y, seed=42)
        >>> _ = se.evaluate_expr(["C", "*", "X_1", "-", "X_0"])
        >>> print(se.get_metric(["C", "*", "X_1", "-", "X_0"], "r2") > 0.999)
        True
        >>> # A custom measure: worst-case absolute residual.
        >>> def max_abs_residual(predict, X, y):
        ...     return float(np.max(np.abs(predict(X) - y)))
        >>> print(se.get_metric(["C", "*", "X_1", "-", "X_0"], max_abs_residual) < 1e-6)
        True

    Args:
        expr: Expression as a token list in infix notation or a
            [Node][SRToolkit.utils.expression_tree.Node] tree. Must already have been
            passed to ``evaluate_expr``.
        metric: Either the name of a built-in metric in
            [REGRESSION_METRICS][SRToolkit.utils.measures.REGRESSION_METRICS]
            (``"mse"``, ``"rmse"``, ``"mae"``, ``"r2"``, ``"nrmse"``), or a callable with the
            signature ``metric(predict, X, y) -> float`` where ``predict(X) -> y_pred``
            has the fitted constants bound in. Default ``"r2"``.

    Returns:
        The metric value as a float. Returns ``NaN`` in BED mode, for models that could
        not be scored, or if the metric raises during computation.

    Raises:
        ValueError: If ``expr`` has not been evaluated yet, or if ``metric`` is a
            string that is not a known built-in metric.
        TypeError: If ``metric`` is neither a string nor a callable.
    """
    expr_list = _as_tokens(expr, self.symbol_library)
    expr_str = "".join(expr_list)

    index = self._model_index.get(expr_str)
    if index is None:
        raise ValueError(
            f"[SR_evaluator.get_metric] Expression '{expr_str}' has not been evaluated yet. "
            "Call evaluate_expr() on it first so its constants are fitted and cached."
        )

    # Validate the metric up front so unknown names raise regardless of mode.
    if isinstance(metric, str):
        if metric not in REGRESSION_METRICS:
            raise ValueError(
                f"[SR_evaluator.get_metric] Unknown metric '{metric}'. Available built-in metrics: "
                f"{sorted(REGRESSION_METRICS)}. Alternatively pass a callable with signature "
                "metric(predict, X, y) -> float."
            )
    elif not callable(metric):
        raise TypeError(
            f"[SR_evaluator.get_metric] metric must be a string or a callable, got {type(metric).__name__}."
        )

    model = self.models[index]

    # Prediction-based metrics need targets and a fitted model: undefined in BED mode
    # and for models that could not be scored.
    if self.ranking_function != "rmse" or self.y is None:
        return float("nan")
    if model.status != "ok":
        return float("nan")

    backend = str(self.parameter_estimator.estimation_settings["backend"])
    return evaluate_metric(
        expr_list, model.parameters, self.X, self.y, metric, self.symbol_library, backend=backend
    )

def get_results(
    self, approach_name: str = "", top_k: int = 20, results: Optional["SR_results"] = None
) -> "SR_results":
    """Returns the results of the equation discovery/symbolic regression process/evaluation.

    Examples:
        >>> X = np.array([[1, 2], [8, 4], [5, 4], [7, 9], ])
        >>> y = np.array([3, 0, 3, 11])
        >>> se = SR_evaluator(X, y)
        >>> rmse = se.evaluate_expr(["C", "*", "X_1", "-", "X_0"])
        >>> results = se.get_results(top_k=1)
        >>> print(results[0].num_evaluated)
        1
        >>> print(results[0].evaluation_calls)
        1
        >>> print(results[0].best_expr)
        C*X_1-X_0
        >>> print(results[0].min_error < 1e-6)
        True
        >>> print(1.99 < results[0].top_models()[0].parameters[0] < 2.01)
        True

    Args:
        approach_name: The name of the approach used to discover the equations.
        top_k: The number of top results to include in the output. If `top_k`
            is greater than the number of evaluated expressions, all
            evaluated expressions are included. If `top_k` is less than 0,
            all evaluated expressions are included.
        results: An SR_results object containing the results of the previous evaluation. If provided,
            the results of the current evaluation are appended to the existing results. Otherwise, a new SR_results
            object is created.

    Returns:
        An instance of the SR_results object with the results of the evaluation.
    """
    if results is None:
        results = SR_results()

    results.add_results(
        self.models,
        self.trace,
        top_k,
        self.success_threshold,
        approach_name,
        self.metadata,
    )

    return results

def add_results(
    self,
    models: List[ModelResult],
    trace: List[int],
    top_k: int,
    success_threshold: Optional[float],
    approach_name: str,
    metadata: Optional[dict] = None,
) -> None:
    """Adds the results of an evaluation to the results object.

    Args:
        models: Evaluated models in the order they were first evaluated.
        trace: The evaluation trace: the index into ``models`` requested by each counted call.
        top_k: Default number of models returned by ``top_models()``. Negative means all.
        success_threshold: The success threshold used to determine whether the evaluation was successful.
        approach_name: The name of the approach used to discover the equations.
        metadata: A dictionary containing additional metadata about the evaluation.
    """
    dataset_name = None
    remaining_metadata = None
    if metadata is not None and "dataset_name" in metadata:
        dataset_name = metadata["dataset_name"]
        remaining_metadata = {key: value for key, value in metadata.items() if key != "dataset_name"}
        if len(remaining_metadata) == 0:
            remaining_metadata = None
    elif metadata is not None:
        remaining_metadata = metadata

    results_obj = EvalResult(
        all_models=list(models),
        trace=list(trace),
        approach_name=approach_name,
        success_threshold=success_threshold,
        top_k=top_k,
        dataset_name=dataset_name,
        metadata=remaining_metadata,
    )

    self.results.append(results_obj)

def print_results(
    self,
    experiment_number: Optional[int] = None,
    detailed: bool = False,
    model_scope: Literal["best", "top", "all"] = "top",
    augmentations: Optional[List[str]] = None,
):
    r"""Prints the results of the SR_evaluator.

    Displays the minimum error, best expression, evaluation counts, success status,
    metadata, and approach name. When *detailed* is ``True``, also prints per-model
    information. Augmentation data is formatted by the corresponding
    [ResultAugmenter][SRToolkit.evaluation.sr_evaluator.ResultAugmenter] subclass,
    looked up from the global registry via the ``_type`` field stored in each
    augmentation entry.

    Examples:
        >>> X = np.array([[1, 2], [8, 4], [5, 4], [7, 9], ])
        >>> y = np.array([3, 0, 3, 11])
        >>> se = SR_evaluator(X, y, seed=42)
        >>> rmse = se.evaluate_expr(["C", "*", "X_1", "-", "X_0"])
        >>> results = se.get_results(top_k=1)
        >>> results.print_results()  # doctest: +ELLIPSIS
        === Experiment 1/1 ===
        Best expression: C*X_1-X_0
        Error: ...
        Evaluated: 1 expressions | Calls: 1 | Success: ...
        <BLANKLINE>
        >>> results.print_results(detailed=True, experiment_number=0)  # doctest: +ELLIPSIS
        Best expression: C*X_1-X_0
        Error: ...
        Evaluated: 1 expressions | Calls: 1 | Success: ...
        <BLANKLINE>
        Models:
          C*X_1-X_0  (error=..., params=...)
        <BLANKLINE>

    Args:
        experiment_number: Number of the experiment to print. If None, prints all.
        detailed: If True, prints per-model information.
        model_scope: Which models to show when *detailed* is True.
            ``"best"`` shows only the top model, ``"top"`` shows the top-k,
            ``"all"`` shows all evaluated models.
        augmentations: Filter which augmenters to display by name.
            If None, all augmentations present in the data are shown.

    Raises:
        TypeError: If ``experiment_number`` is not an integer.
        IndexError: If ``experiment_number`` is out of range. Negative numbers count from the end.
    """
    if experiment_number is None:
        for i, result in enumerate(self.results):
            print(f"=== Experiment {i + 1}/{len(self.results)} ===")
            SR_results._print_result_(result, detailed, model_scope, augmentations)
            print()
    else:
        SR_results._print_result_(self[experiment_number], detailed, model_scope, augmentations)

def augment(
    self, augmenters: Union[List[ResultAugmenter], ResultAugmenter], experiment_number: Optional[int] = None

    r"""Applies the given [ResultAugmenter][SRToolkit.evaluation.sr_evaluator.ResultAugmenter]

        >>> y = np.array([3, 0, 3, 11])
        >>> se = SR_evaluator(X, y, seed=42)
        >>> rmse = se.evaluate_expr(["C", "*", "X_1", "-", "X_0"])
        >>> results = se.get_results(top_k=1)
        >>> from SRToolkit.evaluation.result_augmentation import ExpressionToLatex
        >>> results.augment([ExpressionToLatex(SymbolLibrary.default_symbols(2))])
        >>> results[0].augmentations["ExpressionToLatex"]["best_expr_latex"]  # doctest: +ELLIPSIS
        '$C_{0} \\cdot X_{1} - X_{0}$'

    Args:
        augmenters: A [ResultAugmenter][SRToolkit.evaluation.sr_evaluator.ResultAugmenter] or a list of [ResultAugmenter][SRToolkit.evaluation.sr_evaluator.ResultAugmenter] objects to apply to the results.
        experiment_number: If provided, apply augmenters only to this experiment's result.
            If None, apply to all results.
    """
    if isinstance(augmenters, ResultAugmenter):
        augmenters = [augmenters]

    if experiment_number is not None:
        assert experiment_number < len(self.results), "[SR_results.augment] experiment number out of bounds"
        for augmenter in augmenters:
            try:
                augmenter.write_results(self.results[experiment_number])
            except Exception as e:
                warnings.warn(f"Error augmenting results with {augmenter.name}, skipping: {e}")
    else:
        for result in self.results:
            for augmenter in augmenters:
                try:
                    augmenter.write_results(result)
                except Exception as e:
                    warnings.warn(f"Error augmenting results with {augmenter.name}, skipping: {e}")

def __getitem__(self, item: int) -> EvalResult:
    """Returns the results of the experiment with the given index.

    Examples:
        >>> X = np.array([[1, 2], [8, 4], [5, 4], [7, 9], ])
        >>> y = np.array([3, 0, 3, 11])
        >>> se = SR_evaluator(X, y)
        >>> rmse = se.evaluate_expr(["C", "*", "X_1", "-", "X_0"])
        >>> results = se.get_results(top_k=1)
        >>> result_of_first_experiment = results[0]

    Args:
        item: the index of the experiment. Negative indices count from the end, as for a list.

    Returns:
        The results of the experiment with the given index.

    Raises:
        TypeError: If ``item`` is not an integer.
        IndexError: If ``item`` is out of range.
    """
    if not isinstance(item, int):
        raise TypeError(f"[SR_results.__getitem__] Index must be an integer, got {type(item).__name__}.")
    if not -len(self.results) <= item < len(self.results):
        raise IndexError(f"[SR_results.__getitem__] Index {item} out of range for {len(self.results)} results.")
    return self.results[item]

def save(self, path: str) -> None:
    """Saves the results to a specific file or directory as JSON.

    If *path* is an existing directory, it writes ``results.json`` inside it.
    If *path* is a file path, it must end with the ``.json`` extension.

    Examples:
        >>> import tempfile
        >>> X = np.array([[1, 2], [8, 4], [5, 4], [7, 9], ])
        >>> y = np.array([3, 0, 3, 11])
        >>> se = SR_evaluator(X, y, seed=42)
        >>> _ = se.evaluate_expr(["C", "*", "X_1", "-", "X_0"])
        >>> results = se.get_results(top_k=1)
        >>> with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as tmpdir:
        ...     results.save(tmpdir + "/my_results/results.json")
        ...     loaded = SR_results.load(tmpdir + "/my_results/results.json")
        ...     print(loaded[0].best_expr)
        C*X_1-X_0

    Args:
        path: Directory path or specific .json file path.

    Raises:
        ValueError: If the path is a file with an extension other than .json.
        OSError: If the directory cannot be created.
        TypeError: If a result holds augmentation or ranking data that cannot be saved (see
            [serialization][SRToolkit.utils.serialization]).
    """
    if os.path.isdir(path):
        target_file = os.path.join(path, "results.json")
    else:
        _, extension = os.path.splitext(path)

        if extension == "":
            target_file = os.path.join(path, "results.json")
        elif extension.lower() == ".json":
            target_file = path
        else:
            raise ValueError(f"Invalid file extension '{extension}'. Results must be saved to a '.json' file.")

    target_dir = os.path.dirname(target_file)
    if target_dir and not os.path.isdir(target_dir):
        os.makedirs(target_dir)

    # 3. Prepare data
    output = {
        "format_version": 1,
        "type": "SR_results",
        "results": [r.to_dict() for r in self.results],
    }

    with open(target_file, "w") as f:
        json.dump(output, f, indent=2)

@staticmethod
def load(path: str) -> "SR_results":
    """Load results previously saved with [save][SRToolkit.evaluation.sr_evaluator.SR_results.save].

    If *path* is a directory, it looks for ``results.json`` inside it.
    If *path* is a file, it must end with the ``.json`` extension.

    Args:
        path: Directory path containing ``results.json`` or path to a specific .json file.

    Returns:
        A new [SR_results][SRToolkit.evaluation.sr_evaluator.SR_results] instance with the loaded data.

    Raises:
        FileNotFoundError: If the specified file or directory does not exist.
        ValueError: If the file extension is not .json or if ``format_version`` is not ``1``.
    """
    if os.path.isdir(path):
        results_path = os.path.join(path, "results.json")
    else:
        _, extension = os.path.splitext(path)
        if extension.lower() != ".json":
            raise ValueError(
                f"Invalid file extension '{extension}'. SR_results can only be loaded from '.json' files."
            )
        results_path = path

    if not os.path.exists(results_path):
        raise FileNotFoundError(f"Could not find results file at: {results_path}")

    with open(results_path, "r") as f:
        data = json.load(f)

    if data.get("format_version", 1) != 1:
        raise ValueError(
            f"[SR_results.load] Unsupported format_version: {data.get('format_version')!r}. Expected 1."
        )

    sr_results = SR_results()
    sr_results.results = [EvalResult.from_dict(r) for r in data["results"]]
    return sr_results

def evaluate_metric(
    expr: Union[List[str], Node],
    parameters: Optional[np.ndarray],
    X: np.ndarray,
    y: np.ndarray,
    metric: Union[str, Callable[[Callable[[np.ndarray], np.ndarray], np.ndarray, np.ndarray], float]] = "r2",
    symbol_library: Optional[SymbolLibrary] = None,
    backend: str = "stack",
) -> float:
    """Score an expression on ``(X, y)`` by reusing already-fitted ``parameters`` — no refitting.

    Builds a constants-bound prediction function ``predict(X) -> y_pred`` from ``expr`` and
    ``parameters`` and applies ``metric``. This is the shared scoring core behind
    [SR_evaluator.get_metric][SRToolkit.evaluation.sr_evaluator.SR_evaluator.get_metric] (train
    data) and [HoldoutMetric][SRToolkit.evaluation.result_augmentation.HoldoutMetric] (held-out
    data) — the same call against different arrays.

    Args:
        expr: Expression as an infix token list or a [Node][SRToolkit.utils.expression_tree.Node].
        parameters: Fitted constants to bind in. ``None`` is treated as an empty array.
        X: Inputs of shape ``(n_samples, n_features)`` to score on.
        y: Targets of shape ``(n_samples,)`` to score against.
        metric: A built-in name in
            [REGRESSION_METRICS][SRToolkit.utils.measures.REGRESSION_METRICS]
            (``"mse"``, ``"rmse"``, ``"mae"``, ``"r2"``, ``"nrmse"``) or a callable
            ``metric(predict, X, y) -> float``.
        symbol_library: Symbol library used to compile ``expr``. Defaults to the package default.
        backend: Compilation backend forwarded to
            [compile_expr][SRToolkit.utils.expression_compiler.compile_expr]. Default ``"stack"``.

    Returns:
        The metric value as a float, or ``NaN`` if the metric raises during computation.

    Raises:
        ValueError: If ``metric`` is a string that is not a known built-in metric.
        TypeError: If ``metric`` is neither a string nor a callable.
    """
    if isinstance(metric, str):
        if metric not in REGRESSION_METRICS:
            raise ValueError(
                f"[evaluate_metric] Unknown metric '{metric}'. Available built-in metrics: "
                f"{sorted(REGRESSION_METRICS)}. Alternatively pass a callable with signature "
                "metric(predict, X, y) -> float."
            )
        metric_fn = REGRESSION_METRICS[metric]
    elif callable(metric):
        metric_fn = metric
    else:
        raise TypeError(f"[evaluate_metric] metric must be a string or a callable, got {type(metric).__name__}.")

    expr_list = _as_tokens(expr, symbol_library)

    raw = compile_expr(expr_list, symbol_library, backend=backend)
    params = parameters if parameters is not None else np.array([])

    def predict(X_in: np.ndarray) -> np.ndarray:
        return raw(X_in, params)

    try:
        with np.errstate(divide="ignore", invalid="ignore", over="ignore", under="ignore"):
            return float(metric_fn(predict, X, y))
    except Exception as e:
        warnings.warn(f"[evaluate_metric] Error computing metric for '{''.join(expr_list)}': {e}")
        return float("nan")

    by ``callback_class``, and delegates to that class's
    [from_dict][SRToolkit.evaluation.callbacks.SRCallbacks.from_dict]. Mirrors
    [SR_dataset.from_dict][SRToolkit.dataset.sr_dataset.SR_dataset.from_dict], which
    resolves its own class the same way.

    Args:
        config: A serialised callback config containing a ``callback_class`` key, as
            produced by
            [to_dict][SRToolkit.evaluation.callbacks.SRCallbacks.to_dict].

    Returns:
        A new instance of the concrete callback class.

    Raises:
        ImportError: If ``callback_class`` cannot be imported (e.g. its ``.srtk`` bundle
            is not installed, or the config has no ``_bundle`` key and was never bound).
    """
    config = _auto_bind(config)
    class_path = config["callback_class"]
    module_path, cls_name = class_path.rsplit(".", 1)
    try:
        target_cls = getattr(importlib.import_module(module_path), cls_name)
    except (ImportError, AttributeError):
        raise ImportError(
            f"Cannot import callback class {class_path!r}. "
            "If this is a bundle class, install the bundle first. "
            "If the config has no '_bundle' key, call bind_config(config) manually."
        ) from None
    return target_cls.from_dict(config)

docs.text:
TimeLimitCallback(time_limit: Union[float, timedelta])

Bases: SRCallbacks

Stops the search once a wall-clock time limit has elapsed.

The timer starts when the experiment begins (on_experiment_start) and uses time.monotonic so it is unaffected by system clock adjustments. The stop request is issued from the next expression evaluation after the limit is exceeded, so the search may run slightly past time_limit depending on how long a single evaluation takes.

Examples:

>>> cb = TimeLimitCallback(time_limit=60.0)
>>> cb.time_limit
60.0
>>> from datetime import timedelta
>>> TimeLimitCallback(time_limit=timedelta(minutes=2)).time_limit
120.0

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default time_limit Union[float, timedelta]

Maximum wall-clock duration before the search is stopped at the next expression evaluation. Either a number of seconds or a datetime.timedelta, which is converted to seconds and stored as a float. Must be strictly positive.

required

Raises:

Type Description ValueError

If time_limit is not strictly positive.

Source code in SRToolkit/evaluation/callbacks.py 
def __init__(self, time_limit: Union[float, timedelta]):
    """Args:
        time_limit: Maximum wall-clock duration before the search is stopped at the next
            expression evaluation. Either a number of seconds or a
            `datetime.timedelta`, which is converted to seconds and stored as a float.
            Must be strictly positive.

    Raises:
        ValueError: If ``time_limit`` is not strictly positive.
    """
    if isinstance(time_limit, timedelta):
        time_limit = time_limit.total_seconds()
    if time_limit <= 0:
        raise ValueError(f"time_limit must be strictly positive, got {time_limit}.")
    self.time_limit: float = time_limit
    self._start_time: Optional[float] = None

docs.title: LoggingCallback
docs.text:
LoggingCallback(log_file: Optional[str] = None)

Bases: SRCallbacks

Logs each new best expression to stdout or a file.

log_file may contain placeholders that are resolved at experiment start using fields from ExperimentEvent. Available placeholders: {dataset_name},{approach_name}, {seed}. Using per-experiment placeholders (e.g. {seed}) gives each job its own file, which is the recommended approach for parallel execution.

When multiple jobs share the same resolved file path, writes are protected by fcntl.flock (POSIX advisory locking) so concurrent processes on Linux / macOS do not corrupt each other's output. On Windows or network filesystems where flock is unavailable the lock is silently skipped.

Examples:

>>> cb = LoggingCallback()
>>> cb.on_best_expression(BestExpressionFound("Nguyen-1_ProGED_42", "X_0+C", 0.001, 10))
[Experiment Nguyen-1_ProGED_42] New best: X_0+C (error=1.000000e-03)
>>> cb = LoggingCallback(log_file="logs/{dataset_name}_{seed}.log")
>>> cb.on_experiment_start(ExperimentEvent(dataset_name="test", max_evaluations=10, seed=1,
...                                        success_threshold=0, approach_name="ta"))
>>> cb._resolved_log_file
'logs/test_1.log'

log_file: Destination for log messages. If None, messages are printed to stdout. May be a plain path or a template string with placeholders {dataset_name}, {approach_name}, {seed} that are resolved when the experiment starts.

Source code in SRToolkit/evaluation/callbacks.py

        that are resolved when the experiment starts.

def on_best_expression(self, event: BestExpressionFound) -> None:
    log_msg = f"[Experiment {event.experiment_id}] New best: {event.expression} (error={event.error:.6e})\n"
    if self._resolved_log_file is not None:
        os.makedirs(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(self._resolved_log_file)), exist_ok=True)
        with open(self._resolved_log_file, "a") as f:
            try:
                import fcntl

                fcntl.flock(f, fcntl.LOCK_EX)
                f.write(log_msg)
                fcntl.flock(f, fcntl.LOCK_UN)
            except (ImportError, OSError):
                f.write(log_msg)
    else:
        print(log_msg, end="")

def __init__(
    self,
    X: np.ndarray,
    y: np.ndarray,
    symbol_library: Optional[SymbolLibrary] = None,
    seed: Optional[int] = None,
    **kwargs: Unpack[RankingSettings],
) -> None:
    """Fits free constants in symbolic expressions by minimizing RMSE against target values.

    Examples:
        >>> X = np.array([[1, 2], [8, 4], [5, 4], [7, 9]])
        >>> y = np.array([3, 0, 3, 11])
        >>> pe = ParameterEstimator(X, y)
        >>> rmse, constants = pe.estimate_parameters(["C", "*", "X_1", "-", "X_0"])
        >>> print(rmse < 1e-6)
        True
        >>> print(1.99 < constants[0] < 2.01)
        True

    Args:
        X: Input data of shape ``(n_samples, n_features)`` used to evaluate expressions.
        y: Target values of shape ``(n_samples,)``.
        symbol_library: Symbol library defining the token vocabulary.
            Defaults to [SymbolLibrary.default_symbols][SRToolkit.utils.symbol_library.SymbolLibrary.default_symbols].
        seed: Random seed for reproducible constant initialization. Default ``None``.
        **kwargs: Optional estimation settings from
            [RankingSettings][SRToolkit.utils.types.RankingSettings].
            Supported keys: ``method``, ``tol``, ``gtol``, ``max_iter``,
            ``constant_bounds``, ``initialization``, ``max_constants``,
            ``max_expr_length``, ``backend``.

    Raises:
        ValueError: If ``constant_bounds`` is not a ``(lower, upper)`` pair, ``backend`` is not
            one of the supported values, or ``max_constants`` / ``max_expr_length`` is not an
            ``int`` or numpy integer (``bool`` is rejected).

    Attributes:
        symbol_library: The symbol library used.
        X: Input data.
        y: Target values.
        seed: Random seed.
        estimation_settings: Active settings dict, merged from defaults and ``**kwargs``.
    """
    if symbol_library is None:
        symbol_library = SymbolLibrary.get_or_default()
    self.symbol_library = symbol_library
    self.X = X
    self.y = y
    self.seed = seed

    self.estimation_settings = dict(DEFAULT_ESTIMATION_SETTINGS)

    if kwargs:
        for k in self.estimation_settings.keys():
            if k in kwargs:
                self.estimation_settings[k] = kwargs[k]  # type: ignore[literal-required]

    for key in ("max_constants", "max_expr_length"):
        value = self.estimation_settings[key]  # type: ignore[literal-required]
        self.estimation_settings[key] = _validate_limit(value, key, allow_negative=True)  # type: ignore[literal-required]

    bounds = self.estimation_settings["constant_bounds"]
    if not (isinstance(bounds, (tuple, list, np.ndarray)) and len(bounds) == 2):
        raise ValueError(f"constant_bounds must be a (lower, upper) pair, got {bounds!r}")
    self.estimation_settings["constant_bounds"] = (bounds[0], bounds[1])

    if self.estimation_settings["backend"] not in ("stack", "codegen", "stack_py"):
        raise ValueError(
            f"backend must be 'stack', 'codegen', or 'stack_py', got {self.estimation_settings['backend']!r}"
        )

    self._rng = np.random.default_rng(self.seed)

    [SR_evaluator][SRToolkit.evaluation.sr_evaluator.SR_evaluator] enforces its own required

        >>> X = np.array([[1, 2], [8, 4], [5, 4], [7, 9]])
        >>> y = np.array([3, 0, 3, 11])
        >>> pe = ParameterEstimator(X, y)
        >>> rmse, constants = pe.estimate_parameters(["C", "*", "X_1", "-", "X_0"])
        >>> print(rmse < 1e-6)
        True

        True
        >>> # Constant-free expressions are evaluated directly
        >>> rmse, constants = pe.estimate_parameters(["X_1", "-", "X_0"])
        >>> constants.size

def estimate_parameters_with_info(self, expr: Union[List[str], Node]) -> Tuple[float, np.ndarray, Dict[str, Any]]:
    """Like [estimate_parameters][SRToolkit.evaluation.parameter_estimator.ParameterEstimator.estimate_parameters],
    but also reports how the optimizer ended.

    The returned error is the lowest finite RMSE the optimizer evaluated, with the constants
    that gave it, rather than the optimizer's final value. When a step leaves the region where
    the expression is defined (e.g. ``sqrt(C - X_0)`` with ``C < X_0``), L-BFGS-B aborts and
    reports ``NaN`` even though it had already found good constants.

    Examples:
        >>> X = np.array([[1, 2], [8, 4], [5, 4], [7, 9]])
        >>> y = np.array([3, 0, 3, 11])
        >>> pe = ParameterEstimator(X, y, seed=0)
        >>> rmse, constants, info = pe.estimate_parameters_with_info(["C", "*", "X_1", "-", "X_0"])
        >>> sorted(info)
        ['converged', 'evaluations', 'iterations']
        >>> info["converged"], info["evaluations"] >= info["iterations"]
        (True, True)
        >>> pe.estimate_parameters_with_info(["X_1", "-", "X_0"])[2]
        {}

    Args:
        expr: Expression as a token list in infix notation or a
            [Node][SRToolkit.utils.expression_tree.Node] tree.

    Returns:
        A 3-tuple ``(rmse, parameters, info)``. ``info`` is empty when the optimizer did not
        run (no free constants, or a violated limit). Otherwise it holds:

        - ``converged``: ``scipy``'s ``success`` flag;
        - ``evaluations``: RMSE computations (``nfev``), finite-difference gradient included;
        - ``iterations``: optimizer iterations (``nit``);
        - ``message``: the optimizer's message, only when ``converged`` is ``False``.

        ``converged=False`` does not mean a bad fit: RMSE has no gradient at a
        perfect fit, so L-BFGS-B often ends with ``"ABNORMAL"`` right at the optimum (about 1
        in 10 random starts for an exact fit). Judge a fit by its error.
    """
    # Count on the infix token list, brackets included, as SR_evaluator does, so both apply the
    # limits identically. (For a Node, len() would count tree nodes, without brackets.)
    tokens = _as_tokens(expr, self.symbol_library)
    num_constants = _count_constants(tokens, self.symbol_library)
    if 0 <= self.estimation_settings["max_constants"] < num_constants:
        return np.nan, np.array([]), {}
    if 0 <= self.estimation_settings["max_expr_length"] < len(tokens):
        return np.nan, np.array([]), {}

    executable_error_fn = compile_expr_rmse(
        expr,
        self.symbol_library,
        backend=str(self.estimation_settings["backend"]),
        X=self.X if num_constants > 0 else None,
    )

    if num_constants == 0:
        rmse = executable_error_fn(self.X, np.array([]), self.y)
        return rmse, np.array([]), {}
    else:
        return self._optimize_parameters(executable_error_fn, num_constants)

Pluggable ranking functions for SR_evaluator.

A RankingFunction turns an expression into a single lower-is-better scalar. Built-ins are RMSERanking (alias "rmse") and BEDRanking (alias "bed"); custom rankings are referenced by their fully-qualified import path.

docs.title: RankingResult dataclass
docs.text:
RankingResult(score: float, parameters: Optional[ndarray] = None, extra: Dict[str, Any] = dict(), status: Optional[Literal['rejected', 'undefined']] = None, status_detail: Optional[str] = None)

The outcome of scoring a single expression with a RankingFunction.

Examples:

>>> r = RankingResult(score=0.5, parameters=np.array([1.0, 2.0]))
>>> r.score
0.5
>>> r.parameters.tolist()
[1.0, 2.0]
>>> RankingResult(score=float("nan")).parameters is None
True

Attributes:

Name Type Description score float

The lower-is-better scalar. It becomes the model's error when the status is "ok", and so drives ordering, the success_threshold comparison and best-tracking; with any other status the error is +inf and the score is ignored.

parameters Optional[ndarray]

Fitted constants (RMSE). None when the ranking fits nothing (BED). This is threaded into ModelResult.parameters and reused for held-out scoring.

extra Dict[str, Any]

Freeform, ranking-owned payload for anything beyond parameters (diagnostics, auxiliary fitted arrays, …). Threaded into ModelResult.ranking_data; its values must be ones that can be saved (see serialization), or saving the results raises TypeError. A ranking that wants typed richness may instead subclass RankingResult; the evaluator reads only score, parameters, status and status_detail.

status Optional[Literal['rejected', 'undefined']]

Set only when the ranking knows that it could not score the expression: "rejected" (the expression breaks a rule the ranking enforces) or "undefined" (it has no finite score). Leave it None and the evaluator decides: a finite score is "ok", anything else "undefined". "invalid" and "error" cannot be set here: the evaluator marks unparseable expressions "invalid" before score is called, and a ranking reports an "error" by raising an exception. See Status.

status_detail Optional[str]

The reason, stored as ModelResult.status_detail. Optional; without it the evaluator writes a generic one (e.g. "rmse score is nan").

Ranks expressions by the root-mean-squared error of the best constant fit.

Owns a ParameterEstimator (built in setup); score returns the RMSE together with the fitted parameters, and in extra (stored as ModelResult.ranking_data) how the fit went: whether the optimizer converged, how many RMSE evaluations and iterations it took, and its message when it did not converge. extra is empty when no constants were fitted. def setup(
    self,
    X: np.ndarray,
    y: Optional[np.ndarray],
    ground_truth: Optional[Union[List[str], Node]],
    symbol_library: SymbolLibrary,
    seed: Optional[int],
    settings: Dict[str, Any],
) -> None:
    """Build the parameter estimator that fits each expression's constants to ``y``.

    Args:
        X: Input data of shape ``(n_samples, n_features)``.
        y: Target values. If ``None``, they are generated by evaluating ``ground_truth`` on
            ``X``, which then must contain no free constants.
        ground_truth: Target expression; used only to generate ``y`` when it is missing.
        symbol_library: Token vocabulary.
        seed: Seed for the random initial values of the constants.
        settings: Estimation settings (``method``, ``tol``, ``constant_bounds``,
            ``max_constants``, …); other keys are ignored.

    Raises:
        ValueError: If neither ``y`` nor ``ground_truth`` is given, or ``y`` must be generated
            from a ground truth that contains a free constant.
    """
    if y is None:
        if ground_truth is None:
            raise ValueError(
                "RMSE ranking requires either target values y or a ground truth expression to generate them from."
            )
        y = self._targets_from_ground_truth(X, ground_truth, symbol_library)
    self.parameter_estimator = ParameterEstimator(X, y, symbol_library=symbol_library, seed=seed, **settings)

docs.title: BEDRanking
docs.text:
Bases: RankingFunction

Ranks expressions by their Behavior-aware Expression Dissimilarity (BED) to a target behavior.

BED compares what two expressions do rather than how they are written. Each expression is evaluated at a fixed set of points bed_X under num_consts_sampled random draws of its free parameters (within constant_bounds), and the output distributions at each point are compared with the target behavior there. No parameters are fitted, so score returns only the distance and parameters is None. See bed.

setup fixes the points bed_X and the target behavior once. The target behavior comes from the first available of:

  1. A precomputed bed_gt matrix, one row per row of X and num_consts_sampled columns. If a ground_truth is also given, it is used only for the default threshold.
  2. The ground_truth expression, possibly with free parameters, evaluated over bed_X. With samplers (the input distribution, one Sampler per variable) and num_points_sampled > 0, the points are num_points_sampled fresh draws from them; otherwise they are rows of X.
  3. The observed targets y, treated as a deterministic behavior. This lets BED rank expressions on measured data with no known expression.

For bed_gt and y, the behavior is known only at the rows of X, so the points are rows of X (the same rows are kept in the behavior) and samplers are not used. Rows of X are subsampled without replacement to num_points_sampled; -1 uses all of them, which is how to score on exactly a given set of points.

All randomness (points, behavior matrices, threshold) follows one seed: the ranking_seed setting when given, otherwise the evaluator's seed. SR_dataset.create_evaluator sets ranking_seed to the dataset's seed, so every run on a dataset is scored by the same objective, unless bed_resample=True.

The default success threshold is the ground truth's own noise floor: its largest BED to itself over 100 resamplings of its free parameters, times 1.1. Without a ground-truth expression there is nothing to resample, so there is no default threshold; set one.

def setup(
    self,
    X: np.ndarray,
    y: Optional[np.ndarray],
    ground_truth: Optional[Union[List[str], Node]],
    symbol_library: SymbolLibrary,
    seed: Optional[int],
    settings: Dict[str, Any],
) -> None:
    """Fix the evaluation points and the target behavior that expressions are compared against.

    See the class description for the order in which the target behavior (``bed_gt``,
    ``ground_truth``, ``y``) and the points (``samplers`` or rows of ``X``) are chosen.

    Args:
        X: Input data of shape ``(n_samples, n_features)``; the points are taken from its rows
            unless samplers are used.
        y: Observed targets, used as the target behavior when neither ``bed_gt`` nor
            ``ground_truth`` is given.
        ground_truth: Target expression, possibly with free parameters.
        symbol_library: Token vocabulary.
        seed: Seed for all of BED's randomness, unless ``settings`` has a ``ranking_seed``.
        settings: BED settings (``num_points_sampled``, ``num_consts_sampled``,
            ``constant_bounds``, ``samplers``, ``bed_gt``, ``ranking_seed``, ``backend``); other
            keys are ignored.

    Raises:
        ValueError: If no target behavior can be built, or if ``ground_truth``, ``bed_gt``,
            ``y`` or ``samplers`` do not fit ``X`` (wrong type, shape or count).
    """
    # Runtime guard: configs loaded from JSON bypass the annotation, so a string or array can get here.
    if ground_truth is not None and not isinstance(ground_truth, (list, Node)):
        raise ValueError("Ground truth must be provided as a list of tokens or a Node object.")  # pyright: ignore[reportUnreachable]

    self.ground_truth = ground_truth
    self.symbol_library = symbol_library
    # All of BED's randomness (points, behaviour matrices, threshold) follows one seed: an
    # explicit ranking_seed (fixed per dataset) or else the evaluator's seed.
    ranking_seed = settings.get("ranking_seed")
    self.seed = ranking_seed if ranking_seed is not None else seed
    self.num_consts_sampled = settings.get("num_consts_sampled", 32)
    self.num_points_sampled = settings.get("num_points_sampled", 64)
    self.constant_bounds = settings.get("constant_bounds", (-5, 5))
    self.backend = settings.get("backend", "stack")
    samplers = settings.get("samplers", None)

    # The behaviour to compare against, in order: a precomputed bed_gt matrix, the ground-truth
    # expression, or the observed targets y (a deterministic behaviour).
    bed_gt = settings.get("bed_gt", None)
    row_behavior: Optional[np.ndarray] = None
    if bed_gt is not None:
        row_behavior = np.asarray(bed_gt)
        self._validate_bed_gt(row_behavior, X)
    elif ground_truth is not None:
        pass  # behaviour is computed from the expression below
    elif y is not None:
        y = np.asarray(y)
        if y.ndim != 1 or y.shape[0] != X.shape[0]:
            raise ValueError(
                f"Targets y must be 1-D with one value per row of X ({X.shape[0]}), got shape {y.shape}."
            )
        row_behavior = np.repeat(y[:, None], self.num_consts_sampled, axis=1)
    else:
        raise ValueError(
            "The bed ranking function requires a ground truth (a list of tokens or a Node object), "
            "a precomputed bed_gt behaviour matrix, or target values y."
        )

    if row_behavior is not None:
        # A matrix or y describes behaviour at the rows of X, so the points are rows of X, and
        # any subsampling applies the same rows to both. Samplers would need behaviour at fresh
        # points, which neither has, so they are not used.
        indices = self._subsample_rows(X.shape[0])
        self.bed_X = X[indices, :]
        self.gt_behavior = row_behavior[indices, :]
        return

    # Ground-truth expression: points drawn from the samplers, or rows of X when there are none
    # or num_points_sampled=-1 asks for all of X; the behaviour is computed over them.
    if samplers is not None and self.num_points_sampled != -1:
        if len(samplers) != X.shape[1]:
            raise ValueError(f"Got {len(samplers)} samplers for {X.shape[1]} variables; give one per variable.")
        # One sampler per feature; each draws a column (cf. SR_dataset.resample). Samplers
        # draw from the global np.random state, so seed it here for reproducibility.
        if self.seed is not None:
            np.random.seed(self.seed)
        # Imported here: SRToolkit.dataset imports this module.
        from SRToolkit.dataset.sampling import _sample_inputs

        self.bed_X = _sample_inputs(samplers, self.num_points_sampled)
    else:
        self.bed_X = X[self._subsample_rows(X.shape[0]), :]

    # row_behavior is None only when the ground-truth branch above was taken.
    assert ground_truth is not None
    self.gt_behavior = create_behavior_matrix(
        ground_truth,
        self.bed_X,
        num_consts_sampled=self.num_consts_sampled,
        consts_bounds=self.constant_bounds,
        symbol_library=self.symbol_library,
        seed=self.seed,
        backend=self.backend,
    )

def default_success_threshold(self) -> Optional[float]:
    # Estimating the noise floor relies on resampling the ground truth's constants; with only a
    # precomputed bed_gt matrix or targets y there is nothing to resample, so no default exists.
    # (With both bed_gt and a ground truth, the matrix is scored and the expression sets this.)
    if self.ground_truth is None:
        return None
    # Each resampling needs its own constant draws; derive them from the ranking seed so the
    # threshold is reproducible whenever the seed is set.
    seeds = (
        np.random.default_rng(self.seed).integers(0, 2**31 - 1, size=100) if self.seed is not None else [None] * 100
    )
    distances = [
        bed(
            self.ground_truth,
            self.gt_behavior,
            self.bed_X,
            num_consts_sampled=self.num_consts_sampled,
            consts_bounds=self.constant_bounds,
            symbol_library=self.symbol_library,
            seed=None if s is None else int(s),
            backend=self.backend,
        )
        for s in seeds
    ]
    return float(np.max(distances) * 1.1)

def build_ranking(spec: Union[str, RankingFunction], fallback: str = "rmse") -> RankingFunction:
    """Resolve a ranking specification to an (un-``setup``) instance.

    Args:
        spec: A [RankingFunction][SRToolkit.evaluation.ranking.RankingFunction] instance (returned
            as-is), a built-in alias (``"rmse"``, ``"bed"``), or a fully-qualified
            ``"module.ClassName"`` import path resolved via ``importlib``.
        fallback: Alias to fall back to (with a warning) when ``spec`` is an unknown bare name.

    Returns:
        A ranking instance, not yet ``setup``.

    Raises:
        TypeError: If ``spec`` is neither a string nor a ``RankingFunction``.
        ImportError: If an import-path ``spec`` cannot be imported (e.g. its ``.srtk`` bundle
            is not installed).
        ValueError: If an import-path ``spec`` resolves to something that is not a
            ``RankingFunction`` subclass.
    """
    if isinstance(spec, RankingFunction):
        return spec
    if not isinstance(spec, str):
        raise TypeError(
            f"[build_ranking] ranking_function must be a string or a RankingFunction, got {type(spec).__name__}."
        )

    key = spec.lower()
    if key in _RANKING_ALIASES:
        return _RANKING_ALIASES[key]()

    if "." in spec:
        module_path, class_name = spec.rsplit(".", 1)
        try:
            klass = getattr(importlib.import_module(module_path), class_name)
        except (ImportError, AttributeError):
            raise ImportError(
                f"Cannot import ranking class {spec!r}. "
                "If this is a bundle class, install the bundle first. "
                "If the config has no '_bundle' key, call bind_config(config) manually."
            ) from None
        if not (isinstance(klass, type) and issubclass(klass, RankingFunction)):
            raise ValueError(f"[build_ranking] '{spec}' is not a RankingFunction subclass.")
        return klass()

    warnings.warn(f"ranking_function '{spec}' not supported. Using {fallback} instead.")
    return _RANKING_ALIASES[fallback]()

def write_results(self, results: EvalResult) -> None:
    """Write LaTeX representations into *results* and its models.

    Stores ``{"best_expr_latex": ...}`` in
    [EvalResult][SRToolkit.utils.types.EvalResult] ``augmentations``.
    Also stores ``{"expr_latex": ...}`` in each model's augmentations when
    ``scope`` is ``"top"`` or ``"all"``.

    Args:
        results: The [EvalResult][SRToolkit.utils.types.EvalResult] to augment.
    """
    eval_data: Dict[str, Any] = {}
    try:
        eval_data["best_expr_latex"] = tokens_to_tree(results.top_models(1)[0].expr, self.symbol_library).to_latex(
            self.symbol_library
        )
    except Exception as e:
        if self.verbose:
            warnings.warn(f"Unable to convert best expression to LaTeX: {e}")
    results.add_augmentation(self.name, eval_data, self._type)

    scoped = results.all_models if self.scope == "all" else results.top_models() if self.scope == "top" else []
    for model in scoped:
        try:
            model.add_augmentation(
                self.name,
                {"expr_latex": tokens_to_tree(model.expr, self.symbol_library).to_latex(self.symbol_library)},
                self._type,
            )
        except Exception as e:
            if self.verbose:
                warnings.warn(f"Unable to convert expression {''.join(model.expr)} to LaTeX: {e}")

def write_results(self, results: EvalResult) -> None:
    """Write simplified expressions into *results* and its models.

    Stores ``{"simplified_best_expr": ...}`` in
    [EvalResult][SRToolkit.utils.types.EvalResult] ``augmentations`` if
    simplification succeeds. Also stores ``{"simplified_expr": ...}`` in each model's
    augmentations when ``scope`` is ``"top"`` or ``"all"``.

    Args:
        results: The [EvalResult][SRToolkit.utils.types.EvalResult] to augment.
    """
    eval_data: Dict[str, Any] = {}
    try:
        simplified_expr = simplify(results.top_models(1)[0].expr, self.symbol_library)
        if isinstance(simplified_expr, list):
            eval_data["simplified_best_expr"] = "".join(simplified_expr)
        elif isinstance(simplified_expr, Node):
            eval_data["simplified_best_expr"] = "".join(simplified_expr.to_list(self.symbol_library))
        else:
            raise Exception(f"Simplified expression is not a list or Node: {simplified_expr}")
    except Exception as e:
        if self.verbose:
            warnings.warn(f"Unable to simplify {results.best_expr}: {e}")
    results.add_augmentation(self.name, eval_data, self._type)

    scoped = results.all_models if self.scope == "all" else results.top_models() if self.scope == "top" else []
    for model in scoped:
        model_data: Dict[str, Any] = {}
        try:
            simplified_expr = simplify(model.expr, self.symbol_library)
            if isinstance(simplified_expr, list):
                model_data["simplified_expr"] = "".join(simplified_expr)
            elif isinstance(simplified_expr, Node):
                model_data["simplified_expr"] = "".join(simplified_expr.to_list(self.symbol_library))
            else:
                raise Exception(f"Simplified expression is not a list or Node: {simplified_expr}")
        except Exception as e:
            if self.verbose:
                warnings.warn(f"Unable to simplify {''.join(model.expr)}: {e}")
        model.add_augmentation(self.name, model_data, self._type)

HoldoutMetric(data: Union[DataSplit, Tuple[ndarray, ...]], metric: Union[str, Callable[[Callable[[ndarray], ndarray], ndarray, ndarray], float], RankingFunction] = 'rmse', scope: str = 'top', symbol_library: Optional[SymbolLibrary] = None, ground_truth: Optional[Union[list, Node]] = None, ranking_settings: Optional[Dict[str, Any]] = None, seed: Optional[int] = 0, refit_constants: bool = False, name: str = 'HoldoutMetric')

Bases: ResultAugmenter

Scores a result's models on held-out data.

Use it to measure how the expressions found by a search perform on data the search never saw. Apply it with SR_results.augment; it adds the score of the best model to the EvalResult and, depending on scope, to each model.

The kind of score depends on metric:

  • A built-in metric name or a callable ("rmse", "r2", "nrmse", "mae", "mse", or metric(predict, X, y) -> float): each model is evaluated on the held-out X with the constants fitted during the search, and compared with the held-out y. This measures how well the fitted model generalizes. Models without fitted constants (e.g. from a BED search) have them fitted on the held-out data first. With refit_constants=True, every model's constants are fitted on the held-out data, which measures how well the expression's form fits new data instead; these values are marked as refit. Requires y.
  • A RankingFunction: the ranking is set up on the held-out data and scores each model, e.g. BED on the held-out X.

With every kind of metric, models the search could not score (any status other than "ok", e.g. rejected by a required constraint) get NaN; they are not scored on the held-out data.

Examples:

>>> from SRToolkit.evaluation import SR_evaluator
>>> X = np.array([[1.0, 2.0], [8.0, 4.0], [5.0, 4.0], [7.0, 9.0]])
>>> se = SR_evaluator(X, 2 * X[:, 1] - X[:, 0], seed=42)
>>> _ = se.evaluate_expr(["C", "*", "X_1", "-", "X_0"])
>>> results = se.get_results(top_k=1)
>>> X_test = np.array([[2.0, 3.0], [4.0, 1.0], [0.0, 5.0]])
>>> results.augment(HoldoutMetric((X_test, 2 * X_test[:, 1] - X_test[:, 0]), metric="rmse"))
>>> bool(results[0].augmentations["HoldoutMetric"]["best_value"] < 1e-6)
True

def __init__(
    self,
    data: "Union[DataSplit, Tuple[np.ndarray, ...]]",
    metric: Union[
        str, Callable[[Callable[[np.ndarray], np.ndarray], np.ndarray, np.ndarray], float], RankingFunction
    ] = "rmse",
    scope: str = "top",
    symbol_library: Optional[SymbolLibrary] = None,
    ground_truth: Optional[Union[list, Node]] = None,
    ranking_settings: Optional[Dict[str, Any]] = None,
    seed: Optional[int] = 0,
    refit_constants: bool = False,
    name: str = "HoldoutMetric",
) -> None:
    """Scores a result's models on held-out data.

    Use it to measure how the expressions found by a search perform on data the search never
    saw. Apply it with [SR_results.augment][SRToolkit.evaluation.sr_evaluator.SR_results.augment];
    it adds the score of the best model to the
    [EvalResult][SRToolkit.utils.types.EvalResult] and, depending on ``scope``, to each model.

    The kind of score depends on ``metric``:

    - **A built-in metric name or a callable** (``"rmse"``, ``"r2"``, ``"nrmse"``, ``"mae"``,
      ``"mse"``, or ``metric(predict, X, y) -> float``): each model is evaluated on the
      held-out ``X`` with the constants fitted during the search, and compared with the
      held-out ``y``. This measures how well the fitted model generalizes. Models without
      fitted constants (e.g. from a BED search) have them fitted on the held-out data first.
      With ``refit_constants=True``, every model's constants are fitted on the held-out data,
      which measures how well the expression's form fits new data instead; these values are
      marked as refit. Requires ``y``.
    - **A [RankingFunction][SRToolkit.evaluation.ranking.RankingFunction]**: the ranking is
      set up on the held-out data and scores each model, e.g. BED on the held-out ``X``.

    With every kind of metric, models the search could not score (any
    [status][SRToolkit.utils.types.Status] other than ``"ok"``, e.g. rejected by a required
    constraint) get ``NaN``; they are not scored on the held-out data.

    Examples:
        >>> from SRToolkit.evaluation import SR_evaluator
        >>> X = np.array([[1.0, 2.0], [8.0, 4.0], [5.0, 4.0], [7.0, 9.0]])
        >>> se = SR_evaluator(X, 2 * X[:, 1] - X[:, 0], seed=42)
        >>> _ = se.evaluate_expr(["C", "*", "X_1", "-", "X_0"])
        >>> results = se.get_results(top_k=1)
        >>> X_test = np.array([[2.0, 3.0], [4.0, 1.0], [0.0, 5.0]])
        >>> results.augment(HoldoutMetric((X_test, 2 * X_test[:, 1] - X_test[:, 0]), metric="rmse"))
        >>> bool(results[0].augmentations["HoldoutMetric"]["best_value"] < 1e-6)
        True

    Args:
        data: The held-out data: a [DataSplit][SRToolkit.dataset.data_split.DataSplit]
            (e.g. ``dataset.test``) or an ``(X[, y])`` tuple.
        metric: A built-in metric name, a callable, or a ``RankingFunction`` (see above).
            Built-in names and callables are computed against the held-out ``y``, so ``data``
            must include it. Measures that need only the expression (e.g. complexity) belong in
            a ``RankingFunction`` or a separate augmenter. Default ``"rmse"``.
        scope: Which models to score: ``"best"``, ``"top"`` (the result's top models), or
            ``"all"``. Default ``"top"``.
        symbol_library: Symbol library used to compile expressions. Defaults to the active
            library.
        ground_truth: Ground-truth expression passed to a ``RankingFunction`` metric's setup
            (e.g. for BED). Unused otherwise.
        ranking_settings: Settings for a ``RankingFunction`` metric's setup and for fitting
            constants on the held-out data (e.g. ``constant_bounds``, ``max_constants``).
            Pass ``dataset.ranking_settings()`` to fit under the same settings as the search
            (``constant_bounds`` included). ``max_constants`` and ``max_expr_length`` apply only if given here: a
            missing one means no limit, not the estimator's default of 8 constants, because the
            search already enforced its limits (including its required constraints) on every
            model it scored ``"ok"``.
        seed: Seed for the ranking setup (e.g. BED point sampling) and the constant fitting.
            Default ``0``.
        refit_constants: Fit every model's constants on the held-out data instead of reusing
            those from the search. Only for built-in or callable metrics. Default ``False``.
        name: Key under which the values are stored in ``augmentations``. Default
            ``"HoldoutMetric"``.

    Raises:
        ValueError: If ``scope`` is invalid, if a built-in or callable ``metric`` is given
            held-out data without ``y``, or if ``refit_constants=True`` is combined with a
            ``RankingFunction`` metric.
        TypeError: If ``data`` is neither a ``DataSplit`` nor an ``(X[, y])`` tuple, or if
            ``metric`` is not a string, callable, or ``RankingFunction``.
    """
    super().__init__(name)

    if scope not in ["best", "top", "all"]:
        raise ValueError(f"[HoldoutMetric] Invalid scope: {scope}. Must be one of 'best', 'top', 'all'.")
    self.scope = scope
    # Resolve the library once, here, so setup() and the reuse-params path always get a concrete
    # one (the active context-manager library, or the package default).
    if symbol_library is None:
        symbol_library = SymbolLibrary.get_or_default()
    self.symbol_library = symbol_library
    self.metric = metric
    self.seed = seed
    self.refit_constants = refit_constants
    self.ranking_settings: Dict[str, Any] = dict(ranking_settings or {})
    # The search enforced its own limits on every model it scored "ok". Apply only the limits
    # given here: the estimator's defaults (max_constants=8) could reject models the search
    # accepted, e.g. under a required MaxConstants(20).
    self._fit_settings: Dict[str, Any] = {"max_constants": -1, "max_expr_length": -1, **self.ranking_settings}
    self._estimator: Optional[ParameterEstimator] = None

    if isinstance(data, tuple):
        self._X = data[0]
        self._y = data[1] if len(data) > 1 else None
    elif hasattr(data, "arrays"):  # DataSplit (duck-typed to avoid an import cycle)
        self._X, self._y = data.X, data.y
    else:
        raise TypeError(
            f"[HoldoutMetric] data must be a DataSplit or an (X[, y]) tuple, got {type(data).__name__}."
        )

    if isinstance(metric, RankingFunction):
        if refit_constants:
            raise ValueError(
                "[HoldoutMetric] refit_constants applies to string/callable metrics only; a "
                "RankingFunction metric is set up on the data provided and refits constants there "
                "if it uses any (e.g. RMSE); it never uses the constants from the search."
            )
        self._ranking_mode = True
        self._metric_label = metric.name
        # Deep-copy so setup() mutates our own instance, not the caller's (which may be shared
        # with an SR_evaluator or another HoldoutMetric).
        self.metric = copy.deepcopy(metric)
        self.metric.setup(self._X, self._y, ground_truth, symbol_library, seed, self._fit_settings)
    elif isinstance(metric, str):
        self._ranking_mode = False
        self._metric_label = metric
    elif callable(metric):
        self._ranking_mode = False
        self._metric_label = getattr(metric, "__name__", "custom")
    else:
        raise TypeError(
            f"[HoldoutMetric] metric must be a string, a callable, or a RankingFunction, got {type(metric).__name__}."
        )

    # A string/callable metric is computed against held-out targets, and missing model
    # parameters are refit against them too — both need y. Fail fast rather than silently
    # producing NaN for every model.
    if not self._ranking_mode and self._y is None:
        raise ValueError(
            f"[HoldoutMetric] metric {self._metric_label!r} requires held-out targets y, but the "
            "data provided none (a single-element (X,) tuple or a DataSplit without a 'y' array)."
        )

def write_results(self, results: EvalResult) -> None:
    """Write the held-out metric into *results* and its models.

    Stores ``{"best_value", "metric", "refit_constants"}`` on the
    [EvalResult][SRToolkit.utils.types.EvalResult] and ``{"value", "metric", "refit_constants"}``
    on each scoped model.

    Args:
        results: The [EvalResult][SRToolkit.utils.types.EvalResult] to augment.
    """
    # The best model is also in the scoped models, so score each expression once: rescoring would
    # cost a fit each time and, with a refit, could give a different value.
    values: Dict[str, float] = {}

    def value(model: ModelResult) -> float:
        key = "".join(model.expr)
        if key not in values:
            values[key] = self._value(model)
        return values[key]

    best = results.top_models(1)[0]
    results.add_augmentation(
        self.name,
        {"best_value": value(best), "metric": self._metric_label, "refit_constants": self.refit_constants},
        self._type,
    )

    scoped = results.all_models if self.scope == "all" else results.top_models() if self.scope == "top" else []
    for model in scoped:
        model.add_augmentation(
            self.name,
            {"value": value(model), "metric": self._metric_label, "refit_constants": self.refit_constants},
            self._type,
        )

def to_dict(self, base_path: str, name: str) -> dict:
    """Serialize this augmenter. Supported only in reuse-params mode with a built-in (string)
    metric; the held-out arrays are written to ``base_path``.

    Args:
        base_path: Directory to write the held-out ``.npz`` into.
        name: Identifier used for the data filename.

    Returns:
        A dictionary sufficient to recreate the augmenter via
        [from_dict][SRToolkit.evaluation.result_augmentation.HoldoutMetric.from_dict].

    Raises:
        NotImplementedError: If ``metric`` is a callable or a ``RankingFunction`` (not
            serialisable — reconstruct such augmenters manually).
    """
    if not isinstance(self.metric, str):
        raise NotImplementedError(
            "[HoldoutMetric.to_dict] Only a built-in (string) metric is serialisable; "
            "reconstruct callable/RankingFunction holdout metrics manually."
        )
    import os

    if not os.path.isdir(base_path):
        os.makedirs(base_path)
    # Absolute, so loading does not depend on the working directory at save time.
    data_path = os.path.abspath(os.path.join(base_path, f"{name}_holdout.npz"))
    if self._y is not None:
        np.savez(data_path, X=self._X, y=self._y)
    else:
        np.savez(data_path, X=self._X)

    return {
        "format_version": 1,
        "type": "HoldoutMetric",
        "name": self.name,
        "scope": self.scope,
        "metric": self.metric,
        "data": data_path,
        "symbol_library": self.symbol_library.to_dict() if self.symbol_library is not None else None,
        "seed": self.seed,
        "refit_constants": self.refit_constants,
        # Only the constant-fitting settings are used in this (string-metric) mode, and they are
        # all JSON-safe; ranking-only settings such as samplers are not saved.
        "ranking_settings": _to_json_safe(
            {k: v for k, v in self.ranking_settings.items() if k in DEFAULT_ESTIMATION_SETTINGS}
        ),
    }

docs.title: SRToolkit.evaluation.sr_evaluator
docs.text:
Expression evaluation and results management for symbolic regression.

Contains SR_evaluator, which ranks expressions with a RankingFunction (RMSE by default); SR_results, a container for experiment results; and ResultAugmenter, the base class for post-processing results.

docs.title: Evaluation statuses
docs.text:
Each evaluated expression gets a Status and, unless it is "ok", a status_detail saying why. The evaluator checks in this order and stops at the first match:

  1. "invalid": the parser raises an ExpressionParseError.
  2. "rejected": a pre-check of a required constraint fails (see below), so the expression is not scored; or the ranking function rejects it while scoring.
  3. "error": the ranking function, or a check of a required constraint, raises. The evaluator also emits a warning.
  4. "undefined": the ranking function returns a non-finite error.
  5. "rejected": a post-check of a required constraint fails. The fit is kept in parameters.
  6. "ok": otherwise.

Every status except "ok" gets the error +inf, so an evaluated expression never gives NaN and failed models rank after every scored one. Every call counts toward max_evaluations, whatever its status. Once evaluation has stopped (threshold or budget reached), further calls are not evaluated: they warn, return nan and are not counted.

The statuses are saved with the results, so validity can be measured after the run from status_counts. Count every well-formed expression as valid, including rejected and undefined ones, and leave "error" out entirely, because those failures belong to the evaluation, not to the approach:

counts = result.status_counts()  # per unique expression; per="call" counts every call
validity_rate = 1 - counts["invalid"] / (sum(counts.values()) - counts["error"])

docs.title: Constraints
docs.text:
The evaluator enforces the required_constraints and records the advisory ones, which are the constraints of its background knowledge (see below). Both are ExpressionConstraints; that module explains what the checks look at and the two roles. The evaluator calls setup with its symbol library on its own copies, so the instances passed in are not changed.

  • required_constraints: pre-checks run in order after parsing, post-checks in order after an "ok" score. The first failure gives "rejected" with the status_detail "<ClassName>: <message>", e.g. "MaxConstants: 9 constants, limit 8", and the later checks of that stage are not run. The settings max_constants (default 8) and max_expr_length add a MaxConstants and a MaxTokens in front of the list, unless a negative setting disables them or the list already has one of that class (see SR_evaluator), so [] still allows at most 8 constants.
  • advisory_constraints: pre-checks run on every parsed expression, post-checks on every "ok" model. Each failed check is recorded in ModelResult.advisory_violations as a CheckResult with constraint and stage filled in; the error is not affected.

For one expression the order is: parse, advisory pre-checks, required pre-checks, score, required post-checks, advisory post-checks. So rejected models and models with status "error" still carry their advisory pre-check results. Pre-checks get ModelResult.expr (simplified if simplify_expr=True), post-checks the ModelResult. Checks a constraint does not implement are skipped.

A check that raises an exception, or returns something other than a CheckResult (treated as a TypeError), emits a UserWarning and counts as failed, with CheckResult.error set to "<ExceptionType>: <message>". For a required constraint the status is then "error" with the status_detail "<ClassName>.<pre_check|post_check> raised <ExceptionType>: <message>". For an advisory constraint the result is recorded in advisory_violations like any failed check; leave results with error set out when counting violations.

To avoid spending evaluations on expressions that would fail a pre-check, or to filter candidates by the advisory constraints, an approach can call check_constraints first: it runs the pre-checks only and is not billed.

docs.title: Background knowledge
docs.text: The search sees only the evaluator, so the evaluator carries the task's BackgroundKnowledge as background_knowledge. describe and priors give the task as text and as records, the same as the dataset's, e.g. to build an LLM prompt. Neither mentions the answer, but the evaluator does not hide it: ground_truth is a public attribute, which an approach must not read.

docs.title: Evaluation trace
docs.text:
The evaluator records every counted call to evaluate_expr in order, and each EvalResult carries this record as trace: trace[k] is the index into all_models of the expression requested by call k + 1. Cache hits appear as repeated indices, since they count toward max_evaluations; calls made after evaluation stopped are not recorded. Three methods derive the usual fixed-target and fixed-budget quantities from it:

  • best_so_far: the calls at which the best error strictly improved;
  • calls_to_threshold: the number of calls needed to first reach an error below a threshold (success_threshold by default), or None;
  • best_error_within: the best error within each of the given numbers of calls.

A run that never reaches the threshold is censored, not missing: it shows that more than evaluation_calls calls were needed. Keep such runs when aggregating, for example as the fraction of runs solved within each budget:

import numpy as np
from SRToolkit.experiments import ExperimentGrid

grid = ExperimentGrid.load("results/grid.json")
results = grid.load_results("Nguyen-1", "ProGED")

budgets = np.array([100, 1_000, 10_000])  # at most the experiment's max_evaluations
needed = [r.calls_to_threshold() for r in results]
solved = [np.mean([n is not None and n <= b for n in needed]) for b in budgets]

curves = np.stack([r.best_error_within(budgets) for r in results])
median_curve = np.nanmedian(curves, axis=0)

A result does not record max_evaluations or why its search stopped. For a run that stopped early for another reason than reaching the threshold (e.g. a time limit), best_error_within past its last call is only an upper bound, and a None from calls_to_threshold is censored at fewer calls than the budget. If your runs can stop early, check evaluation_calls against the budget before comparing approaches.

Note

ResultAugmenter is defined here rather than in result_augmentation to avoid circular imports.
